title: Baseline retest for cores/bench
Share and width-prune the combinational DIV/REM datapath
motivation:
The only recorded experiment is the baseline: 12.12 fitness at 5.442 MHz,
with a 199.837 ns, 156-cell worst path through forwarding and the execute
ALU. The ALU expresses signed and unsigned division and remainder as four
separate arithmetic expressions. These deep combinational arithmetic
cones are a strong candidate for the unusually low Fmax, and replicating
them also creates placement and routing pressure in the 12,312-LUT design.
A combinational divider optimization can improve clock frequency without
changing CoreMark's cycle count or the pipeline's stall behavior.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the four real DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU expressions with one shared unsigned
magnitude divider that produces quotient and remainder together. Implement
an explicitly unrolled radix-2 restoring recurrence with compile-time
widths: step k consumes the next dividend bit, has a k-bit candidate
remainder, and subtracts only divisor[k-1:0] using a k+1-bit difference.
Accept that subtraction only when its borrow is clear and every omitted
upper divisor bit is zero. Thus the subtractors grow from 1 to 32 bits,
rather than carrying full-width arithmetic through every step. Use the
subtraction's borrow to select the new remainder and emit the quotient
bit, avoiding a separate full-width comparator before the subtraction.

Normalize operands to unsigned magnitudes only for signed DIV/REM, then
restore the quotient sign from the operand-sign XOR and the remainder
sign from the dividend. Select the signed or unsigned quotient/remainder
at the existing ALU output. Preserve divide-by-zero results, INT_MIN/-1,
truncation toward zero, and dividend-signed remainders exactly. Keep all
RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS formulas byte-for-byte equivalent to the baseline.
This is solely a combinational arithmetic refactoring: retain the ALU
interface, execution latency, forwarding, bus handshakes, retirement
width, decoder legality checks, and all other operations. The prediction
is that narrower fused subtract/select steps and one physical divider
reduce the critical arithmetic delay and routing congestion enough to
exceed the 4.6 percent acceptance threshold with unchanged iterations/cycle.

changes.description:
Replace the real division and remainder operators with a shared,
combinational, width-pruned restoring divider. Use statically sized
stages or generate blocks so synthesis sees the narrow subtractors;
never truncate upper divisor bits without the upper-bits-zero guard.
Fuse quotient-bit generation with subtraction borrow detection, share
the magnitude datapath across all four operations, and apply the
required signed correction and RV32M exceptional results. Preserve
the existing ALTOPS branch and leave multiplier and base-ISA logic
unchanged. Validate the result with the ALU suite, formal pipeline
checks and stalled CoreMark cosim, then compare median Gowin Fmax and
fitness against the baseline; a shared cone alone is insufficient
evidence of a speed improvement.

Extend the existing exact RV32M arithmetic vectors with deterministic
randomized DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU checks against an integer-only reference,
all sign combinations, zero divisors, INT_MIN/-1, magnitude divisors
of 0x80000000 and 0xffffffff, dividends smaller than the divisor, and
divisors around each power of two. Include cases with nonzero upper
divisor bits that would fool a truncated early-stage subtraction and
check both quotient and remainder. Retain every existing test.

title: Remove the combinational divide chain with a shared iterative divider
motivation:
The only recorded experiment is the baseline: fitness 12.12, median Fmax
5.442 MHz, and a 199.837 ns worst path containing 156 cells through
forwarding and u_ex/u_alu. There are no prior structural attempts or
recorded lessons for this core. The four combinational division/remainder
operators in alu.sv are the strongest candidate for this exceptionally
deep arithmetic cone. Even infrequent DIV/REM instructions place that
hardware on the shared execute-result path and constrain the clock used
by every instruction. Serializing division should substantially raise
Fmax and reduce LUT pressure, provided its added CoreMark cycles cost
less than the frequency improvement under the existing bus stalls.

forwarding and u_ex/u_alu. There are no prior structural attempts or

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the real-hardware DIV, DIVU, REM, and REMU datapaths with one
clocked radix-2 restoring divider, shared across all four operations.
Capture the fully forwarded operands and operation exactly once when a
valid division instruction can start. Use registered divisor, quotient,
and 33-bit partial remainder; execute one trial subtraction and quotient
bit per cycle for 32 iterations. Register signed-magnitude preparation
and final sign correction separately so neither forms a long chain with
the iterative subtractor. Quotient sign is the operand-sign XOR, while
remainder sign follows the dividend. Handle zero divisor and signed
INT_MIN/-1 explicitly with the existing RV32M bit results. Eliminate all
synthesizable division and modulo operators from the real ALU branch.
Keep base integer operations and the existing multiplier implementation
on their current single-cycle path; this is one change in the structure
of division execution, with no predictor or memory redesign.

Give the internal ALU a start/busy/result-valid/consume handshake. Hold
fetch and ID/EX while division is outstanding, but let older instructions
drain through MEM and WB. When downstream memory is ready, write a fully
cleared EX/MEM bubble while the divider is computing, rather than holding
an older load/store that could be serviced or retired repeatedly. Existing
dmem backpressure still holds EX/MEM and retains WB forwarding payloads
as before. Start only when EX can accept the division, continue an already
started computation independently of bus readiness, and retain its
registered result until EX/MEM accepts it. On that acceptance, transfer
the original instruction, control, PC, destination, and captured forwarded
source values exactly once and release the frontend. Deassert the frontend
divider-wait when a valid result can enter EX/MEM, so ID/EX advances to the
next instruction on that same edge. Keep the divider transaction active
until this acceptance so the held division cannot restart. Gate
redirects and memory requests by valid instructions and clear all bubble
side-effect controls. Preserve the existing load-use and forwarding
ordering for the immediately following dependent instruction.

Preserve the exact RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS formulas in the ALU, using the same
transaction interface with a short registered completion in ALTOPS builds
so the unchanged bounded formal suite can observe retirement. In normal
builds the divider has a fixed finite arithmetic bound, about 35 cycles
including preparation and completion, apart from external dmem stalls.
Preserve nret=1, the core I/O contract, trap rules, retirement ordering,
memory semantics, and all evaluation checks. Validate exact arithmetic
with the existing DIV/REM vectors adapted to the handshake and additional
randomized signed/unsigned comparisons, and exercise pipeline dependencies,
consecutive divides, and result completion during imem/dmem backpressure.
Assess the result with unchanged formal and CoreMark cosimulation/CRC
gates and Gowin timing; a win requires Fmax_new/Fmax_old to exceed
1.046 times cycles_new/cycles_old for the same ten measured iterations.

title: Small tagged next-PC predictor removes taken-control bubbles
motivation:
The baseline always fetches PC+4 and flushes fetch on every taken branch,
JAL, and JALR. IF/ID is combinational rather than a separate pipeline
register, so each redirect loses one instruction opportunity. CoreMark's
repeated loops and calls should make many of these successors predictable.
The recorded timing bottleneck is the forwarded combinational ALU, so a
small parallel fetch predictor can improve iterations/cycle without adding
logic to that arithmetic path. No predictor attempt appears in the history.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one 32-entry direct-mapped, fully tagged next-PC predictor indexed by
fetch PC[6:2]. Each entry contains a valid bit, PC[31:7] tag, an aligned
target address, and a two-bit saturating taken counter. An invalid entry,
tag miss, or counter below 2 predicts PC+4; a hit with counter at least 2
predicts the stored target. Use PC-only combinational lookup in parallel
with instruction fetch, without an additional fetch stage or an imem-data
dependency. Reset valid bits; other entry fields need no reset and must
never influence a prediction while invalid.

Carry the exact predicted successor used to advance the fetch PC through
IF/ID and ID/EX. At EX, keep the existing forwarded branch comparisons,
JAL/JALR target calculation, link value, and alignment/trap behavior.
Compute the actual architectural successor for every valid instruction,
including PC+4 for ordinary instructions and suppressed misaligned control
transfers. Redirect and flush only when this successor differs from the
captured prediction. Correctly predicted taken transfers accept the target
instruction without a bubble; predicted-taken/actually-not-taken and
stale JALR targets recover to the resolved successor. Checking ordinary
instructions as well also repairs stale entries after instruction changes.

Train once when a valid instruction actually advances out of EX, never
while EX/MEM is held by dmem backpressure. Allocate legal, aligned branches
and jumps with their resolved control target, not the fall-through PC of a
not-taken branch. Initialize a conditional branch counter to 2 for taken
or 1 for not taken, then saturate on later outcomes; initialize jumps to 3
and refresh their targets. Replace conflicting tags rather than training
their old counters. Invalidate a matching stale entry when a non-control
instruction resolves, and clear predictor valid bits on an advancing
FENCE.I without changing decoder legality.

Prediction and its metadata must be consumed together only when fetch is
accepted into ID/EX. Load-use and imem stalls hold the fetch PC and cannot
advance speculative state; a dmem stall also preserves ID/EX metadata.
Gate EX repair and training with valid and !stall_ex_mem, then give repair
priority over imem/load-use holds on the release cycle. Preserve the
existing MEM/WB forwarding retention during dmem stalls. Do not add a
return stack, global history, caches, or arithmetic changes. Keep nret=1,
the top-level interface, actual RVFI pc_next, and all correctness gates.

The prediction is approximately 10 percent higher fitness if correctly
predicted taken transfers remove enough counted cycles with little Fmax
loss. Against 4,491,485 baseline counted cycles, equal Fmax requires saving
more than 197,522 cycles to exceed the 4.6 percent acceptance threshold.
The main risks are direct-map conflicts, changing JALR return targets,
predictor mux area/routing, and recovery correctness during bus stalls.
Confirm the benefit with the unmodified CoreMark/cosim and median Gowin
flow; this is an estimate, not a measured performance result.

title: Use validity to kill fetches and shorten the redirect control path
motivation:
The champion's shared iterative divider removed the original deep arithmetic
bottleneck and achieved 104.51 fitness at 46.944 MHz with 4,491,817 counted
CoreMark cycles. Its recorded worst path is now 27.549 ns and 44 cells,
ending at the fetch PC and traversing ID, EX, IF, hazard logic, and IF again.
Fetch currently replaces the instruction with a NOP when EX redirects or
imem is unready. This makes a late redirect control the instruction bits
used for register-file addressing and load-use comparisons, which then
feed frontend holds. No prior micro_opt attempt has addressed this cone;
the earlier combinational-divider refactoring left its own arithmetic
chain dominant. Removing the unnecessary payload dependency should improve
Fmax without adding instruction cycles or changing the memory system.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace fetch's redirect/flush-controlled NOP substitution with a validity
kill: always expose the raw imem instruction payload, and separately mark
it invalid on redirects or missing instruction responses. Drive the
load-use comparator inputs from raw io_imemData[19:15] and [24:20], so
EX redirect never traverses an instruction mux and source comparators
before reaching frontend control. Keep conservative comparisons against
both fields, including fields that are not actual operands, to preserve
existing cycle behavior and isolate this experiment to control-path delay.

In ID, capture valid with the payload and force all decoded side-effect
controls to zero for an invalid fetch. Keep the existing flush-over-hold
behavior and hold complete ID/EX state during downstream or divider waits.
Downstream invalid instructions must remain side-effect-free bubbles:
no forwarding producer, memory operation, divider launch, redirect, WB
write, or retirement may arise from arbitrary invalid payload bits.
Preserve raw instruction, source values, and trap metadata for every
valid instruction, including reserved encodings and alignment faults.

Express PC next-state priority directly as reset, then resolved redirect,
then an independent frontend hold, then PC+4. The hold expression uses
load-use, imem-not-ready, actual dmem backpressure, and divider-wait only;
it must not depend on redirect, flush, or a flush-modified instruction.
Redirect still kills ID/EX and overrides an imem hold on the same edge;
dmem backpressure suppresses EX redirect exactly as today. Keep redirect
as a direct PC-select and validity/flush signal rather than routing it
through source-address masking or stall qualification. Do not register
redirect, add a recovery cycle, introduce prediction, alter arithmetic,
change the pipeline topology, or change the nret=1 top-level interface.

The falsifiable prediction is unchanged counted cycles and at least an
eight percent increase in median Gowin Fmax, yielding about 112.9 fitness.
With unchanged cycles, acceptance needs Fmax above 49.104 MHz, compared
with the champion's 46.944 MHz. Run the unchanged formal, unit, and stalled
CoreMark cosimulation/CRC gates and inspect Gowin's memory-output timing
paths. The improvement must come from eliminating the synthesized
redirect-to-instruction-to-hazard cone, not from RVFI-only pruning or
placement variation. A remaining branch-target or arithmetic path may
limit the gain, so this estimate has medium confidence.

title: Register control-flow redirects at the EX/MEM boundary
motivation:
The current champion scores 104.51 at 46.944 MHz and 4,491,817 counted
CoreMark cycles. Its shared iterative divider removed the old arithmetic
bottleneck; the reported 27.549 ns, 44-cell worst path now runs from the
register file through ID, EX, fetch flushing and hazard logic to the
fetch PC. There is no IF/ID register, and the combinational EX redirect
both selects the PC and replaces the fetched instruction before load-use
detection. This couples forwarded branch resolution to frontend control
within one clock. The prior structural attempt was the successful divider;
no registered-redirect attempt or LESSONS.md exists. The earlier predictor
ran on the old combinational-divider baseline and does not measure this
champion's remaining timing bottleneck.
A fresh make timing TARGET=bench run reproduces placement-option-0 Fmax
of 44.935 MHz and the same worst path: register-file BRAM output through
forwarded rs2, the EX comparison carry chain, fetch instruction masking,
load-use comparison and frontend control to the PC register clock enable.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move all taken BRANCH, JAL and JALR redirects from combinational EX outputs
to the registered EX/MEM boundary. Resolve forwarded operands, branch
conditions, targets, link values and alignment faults in EX exactly as
today, but capture the redirect-valid bit and architectural next PC with
the instruction entering EX/MEM. Drive fetch redirect and younger-stage
cancellation solely from those registers. Reuse the registered pc_next,
branch_taken and jump/trap controls if that avoids duplicate state. There
must be no combinational path from the current EX operand comparators or
JALR adder into fetch redirect, instruction masking or frontend enables.

This changes control-transfer latency rather than instruction throughput:
straight-line code still issues one instruction per ready cycle, while
each taken transfer incurs one additional recovery cycle. In the cycle
when a registered redirect is applied, the branch/jump in EX/MEM must
advance normally to MEM/WB and retire once. Simultaneously kill the younger
instruction currently in EX, clear ID/EX, invalidate the fetched payload,
and install the registered target PC. Suppress every launch or side effect
of that younger EX instruction, especially divider start, divider payload
capture and EX/MEM capture; a wrong-path DIV must never make the redirect
wait for arithmetic completion. A registered redirect must override
load-use, imem-not-ready and a younger divider's tentative wait. Preserve
existing downstream memory transaction holds and WB forwarding retention.

redirect; an older stalled load/store must not cause a held branch to be
lost, applied early or applied more than once. Misaligned or illegal
control transfers retain their existing traps and produce no redirect.

running in this in-order pipeline: suppressing launch during its recovery
cycle is sufficient, and must not cancel or reset a surviving older
divider transaction. Clear or consume pending redirect state exactly
once as the redirecting instruction leaves EX/MEM.

Keep the iterative divider, multiplier, decoder legality policy, memory
protocol, sole RVFI retirement channel and order counter. This proposal

cache or arithmetic redesign. Its expected benefit is a shorter maximum
combinational path and reduced fanout from EX resolution. The principal
performance risk is the extra taken-transfer cycle; another existing
datapath could become the limiting path. For the unchanged ten measured
iterations, acceptance requires Fmax_new / 46.944 to exceed
1.046 * cycles_new / 4491817. Measure both with the unchanged stalled
CoreMark/CRC/cosim gates and median Gowin timing, rather than accepting
a frequency gain alone. The estimated fitness improvement is unmeasured.

title: Instruction-qualified bimodal prediction with one-bit branch recovery
motivation:
The current champion already removes the combinational divide chain and
reaches 46.944 MHz at 4,491,817 counted CoreMark cycles, for fitness 104.51.
Fetch still advances linearly and loses one fetch opportunity on every
taken branch or jump. The previous predictor attempt, hyp-20261005-003-r1s2,
reduced counted cycles to 4,208,674, about 6.3 percent, but retained the old
combinational divider and its 193.856 ns arithmetic path. That experiment
does not establish predictor timing on the iterative-divider champion.
The champion's worst path now runs through decode, execute, fetch, and
hazard control. A compact direction predictor can remove recurring branch
bubbles while keeping recovery simpler than a tagged next-PC comparison.
No LESSONS.md exists and this is the only recorded predictor attempt.
A read-only run of the unchanged RV32IM reference interpreter on the
canonical CoreMark ELF counted 529,588 conditional branches (294,425
taken), 49,367 JALs, and 13,735 JALRs between the MMIO markers. Updating
weakly-taken bimodal counters immediately after each architectural branch
produced 51,854 direction misses for 64 entries versus 54,457 for 128.
Choose 64 entries for the shorter lookup and lower state cost. This
profile measures direction behavior, not speculative pipeline timing.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Starting from the supplied iterative-divider champion, add one 64-entry
bimodal conditional-branch direction table indexed by fetch PC[7:2]. Each
entry is a two-bit saturating counter, reset to weakly taken (2'b10).
Qualify lookup with the raw fetched instruction: only opcode 0x63 with
funct3 in {0,1,4,5,6,7} is a conditional branch. For an aligned direct
branch, predict taken when the selected counter's high bit is set and
compute its target as fetch PC plus the sign-extended B immediate. Predict
every aligned JAL directly from its J immediate, including its first
execution. Other instructions, JALR, reserved branch encodings, and direct
transfers with misaligned targets predict PC+4. Keep this predecode local
to fetch; the existing validated decoder remains the authority for traps
and side effects. The instruction qualification makes table aliasing
affect direction accuracy only: there are no stored targets, tags, BTB,
return stack, global history, or cached instruction assumptions.

Carry a single predicted-taken bit with the exact accepted instruction
through if_id_t and id_ex_t. For legal aligned conditional branches, EX
computes a repair from actual-taken XOR predicted-taken. A repair selects
the existing branch target for a missed taken prediction, or PC+4 for a
predicted-taken branch that actually falls through. An aligned JAL was
predicted to its exact immediate target and needs no redirect or bubble;
its PC+4 link write remains unchanged. JALR retains the current forwarded
target computation and redirect penalty. Suppressed misaligned transfers
still retire with the existing trap behavior and architectural PC+4.
Keep RVFI pc_next computed from actual execution, independent of prediction.
There is no full-width predicted-next-PC equality check in the conditional
branch recovery path. Derive an effective actual-taken value that includes
the current alignment/trap suppression rather than redirecting on a trap.

Train the selected two-bit counter exactly once when a valid legal aligned
conditional branch advances out of EX. Increment on taken, decrement on
not taken, and saturate at 0 and 3. Use the instruction PC for the write
index and the current table value for updating; simultaneous read/write
observes the pre-edge prediction, which is captured with that instruction.
Do not train on dmem holds, divider waits, invalid bubbles, illegal
encodings, JAL, or JALR. No speculative table writes are needed. Resetting
every counter makes lookup deterministic for symbolic formal streams.

Couple prediction consumption to fetch acceptance: only advance to the
predicted successor on an edge that also captures that instruction into
ID/EX. Never consume a new prediction during load-use, imem, dmem, or
divider waits. Preserve the existing distinct actions: dmem and divider
waits hold ID/EX metadata, load-use injects an ID/EX bubble, and imem
backpressure holds PC while allowing older stages to advance with an
invalid fetch payload. A valid advancing EX repair overrides fetch-side holds and
flushes the one younger fetched instruction. Correct predictions must
leave that younger target instruction valid. Preserve the divider's
start/busy/result-valid/consume interface, its captured operands and
payload, older MEM/WB draining, retained WB forwarding on dmem stalls,
and all real and ALTOPS arithmetic from the current champion.

Integrate recovery without routing the EX repair through an instruction
replacement mux and then back through hazard detection to the PC enable.
Feed load-use comparison from raw io_imemData register fields, qualify it
with io_imemReady, and give an advancing repair explicit priority over
load-use and instruction-bus holds. Use validity and ID flush to discard
wrong-path instructions; the fetch predictor and hazard inputs must not
depend on the redirect-masked NOP. Existing downstream dmem hold priority
remains unchanged, so EX can repair and train only when MEM accepts it.
This is supporting control for the predictor, with no extra pipeline
stage, altered retirement width, memory interface, or arithmetic change.

Expect roughly 8 percent higher fitness from fewer taken-control bubbles
with a small direction table and a one-bit conditional recovery cone.
The architectural profile suggests about 291,938 fewer redirect bubbles
before pipeline-training latency and overlap with bus stalls, equivalent
to 6.5 percent of the champion's counted cycles. The estimate assumes the
simpler repair/hazard path preserves or modestly improves Fmax.
This is an unmeasured estimate; JALR remains a penalty and direction-table
aliases or the imem-to-target-adder path can limit the gain. Validate with
the unchanged formal and CoreMark cosimulation/CRC gates and median Gowin
timing. At unchanged Fmax, acceptance needs counted cycles below about
4,294,280; in general require (Fmax_new / 46.944 MHz) times
(4,491,817 / cycles_new) greater than 1.046. Preserve nret=1, every external
port, exact retirement ordering, decoder legality, and all hard invariants.

title: Preselect ALU operands in decode to shorten the execute input path
motivation:
The current champion scores 117.75 at median Fmax 49.474 MHz and
4,201,709 measured CoreMark cycles. Its 25.054 ns worst path starts at
the register file's inferred block-RAM output, crosses ID operand
handling, EX forwarding and PC/immediate selection, then a multiplier
and result selection before reaching a memory address register.
The prior micro_opt attempts addressed combinational division and
redirect control; neither targets this remaining operand path.
No LESSONS.md exists. A fresh unchanged Gowin build reproduces the
champion's placement-option-0 result, 50.610 MHz and 3,000 logic cells.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move PC-versus-rs1 and immediate-versus-rs2 operand preselection across
the existing ID/EX register boundary, without adding a pipeline stage.
Add two 32-bit fields to id_ex_t. On ordinary ID capture, alu_a_val
receives dec_is_auipc ? fetch_pc : rs1_data and alu_b_val receives
dec_alu_src ? decoded_imm : rs2_data. Use the existing write-first
register-file read data. Capture these fields with the same instruction,
PC, control and validity; retain them on holds and clear them on reset
or flush exactly like the rest of the ID/EX payload.

In EX, replace forwarding followed by PC/immediate selection with one
three-source parallel selection for each ALU operand. For A, enable
EX/MEM forwarding only when !is_auipc and fwd_rs1_sel == 1; enable WB
forwarding only when !is_auipc and fwd_rs1_sel == 2. Select the captured
alu_a_val otherwise. For B, use the same rules with !alu_src and
fwd_rs2_sel, selecting alu_b_val otherwise. Express each operand as
the OR of its three bitwise-masked candidates, with mutually exclusive
enables and the default enable equal to neither forwarding enable.
Thus PC and immediate operands cannot be overwritten by coincidental
raw register-field matches, while a true register operand still sees
the freshest existing EX/MEM-over-WB forwarding decision.

Preserve the separate forwarded architectural rs1 and rs2 networks
for branches, JALR targets, stores and RVFI source values. Feed the
existing ALU and divider launch with the newly selected ALU operands;
preserve the divider's once-only operand/payload capture, completion
and consume protocol. Retained WB data must remain available during
dmem stalls even when WB validity clears. Keep the register-file module,
forwarding priority, hazard controls, prediction, EX/MEM result mux,
pipeline latency, retirement width and all real/ALTOPS arithmetic.
This is one local operand-preselection optimization, with no predictor,
cache, extra execution stage, or additional instruction capability.

An isolated implementation of exactly this operand change has already
completed all three unchanged Gowin placement options: 52.870, 54.400
and 54.400 MHz, giving median Fmax 54.400 MHz, 9.96 percent above the
champion. It uses 3,237 logic cells, 866 registers, 40 LUT-RAM units,
four block RAMs and six DSP units. The inferred register file moves
from block RAM to distributed RAM, and the worst path now starts at
a forwarding tag rather than the register-file block-RAM output.

payload layouts. The unchanged official run_coremark_ipc validator

isolated probe using the official timing and CoreMark functions; the
orchestrator must still run its full formal and correctness gates on
the final implementation. Update test payload layouts rather than
deleting assertions when id_ex_t gains 64 bits.

title: Move multiplication into a registered shared execution unit
motivation:
The champion scores 117.75 at 49.474 MHz and 4,201,709 measured CoreMark
cycles. The iterative divider already removed the original timing
bottleneck. The remaining worst path has 14 cells and 25.054 ns arrival,
from the register file through ID, EX and u_alu to the memory-side
circuit. A fresh unchanged make timing TARGET=bench reproduces placement
option 0 at 50.610 MHz, and its worst five paths all cross multiplier
DSPs. Path 1 crosses u_alu/mult_1287_s1 with 3.760 ns DSP cell delay;
another crosses u_alu/mul_ss_63_s0. These are reached after regfile-output,
forwarding and ALU-input muxes, then drive result selection and dmem
address logic. The arithmetic bottleneck is confirmed, not inferred
solely from module names. Multiplication still uses combinational signed,
unsigned and mixed-sign 64-bit products. There is no LESSONS.md.
The previous structural redirect-register
attempt lost 2.38 percent because it added recovery cycles while the
ALU became limiting; do not repeat that intervention. A read-only run of
the unchanged RV32IM reference interpreter on the canonical CoreMark ELF
counted 2,922,015 retired instructions between the markers, including
93,960 MULs and zero MULH/MULHU/MULHSU or DIV/REM instructions, with no
out-of-bounds access. Optimize the common low-word multiplication latency.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Starting from the supplied champion, remove MUL, MULH, MULHU and MULHSU
from the single-cycle ALU result cone and execute them in one shared,
registered multiplier transaction. Keep ordinary integer operations,
prediction, control-flow recovery, memory behavior and the existing
iterative divider unchanged. Capture the fully forwarded 32-bit source
operands, operation and instruction payload once on a valid unstalled
launch. Feed one unsigned 32-by-32 multiplication exclusively from
these operand registers and capture its full 64-bit product in another
register. MUL and MULHU finish immediately when this product register
is written; select the appropriate registered half directly, without
taking high-word correction states or adding another result-copy cycle.
For MULH and MULHSU, in subsequent registered steps correct the high word using
high_signed = high_unsigned - (signed_a && a[31] ? b : 0)
                            - (signed_b && b[31] ? a : 0), modulo 2^32.
signed_a applies to MULH and MULHSU; signed_b applies only to MULH.
Separate the two 32-bit correction subtractions with a register so they
cannot recreate a long multiply-plus-correction combinational path.
MULHSU needs only the first correction; MULH needs both. A nominal MUL
launched on edge N captures its product and asserts result-valid on
N+1, then is consumed into EX/MEM with frontend release on N+2. Thus
the measured workload pays two extra issue cycles per multiply, rather
than the latency of signed correction for every low-word operation.
Eliminate the original three combinational product expressions from
alu.out; merely registering a selected output after that cone is not
sufficient. This is structural isolation of multiplication latency,
not a change to RV32M arithmetic or the retirement width.

Provide start/busy/result-valid/consume control, analogous to the current
divider. Hold fetch and ID/EX during a multiply, let older MEM/WB work
drain, and write side-effect-free EX/MEM bubbles whenever downstream
memory can advance. Actual dmem stalls still hold EX/MEM and preserve
WB forwarding data. Arithmetic continues independently after launch;
a completed result and its original forwarded operand snapshots remain
stable until downstream acceptance. Transfer the completed payload into
EX/MEM exactly once and release ID/EX on that same edge. Keep busy set
through consumption so the held instruction cannot restart. A following
dependent instruction receives the result through normal forwarding.
Do not launch twice, replay an older memory request, train a held branch,
or allow a waiting instruction's changing forwarding muxes to alter an
outstanding transaction. Reuse the established divider wait/drain

title: Narrow multiply-result prediction with full-width MEM validation
motivation:
The champion scores 117.75 at median Fmax 49.474 MHz and 4,201,709
counted CoreMark cycles. Both prior predictor attempts were reviewed in
log.jsonl; LESSONS.md is absent. The current 64-entry bimodal predictor
already removes most taken-control bubbles. A new read-only architectural
profile found 135,320 immediate load-to-branch dependencies, too few for
their removal alone to exceed the 184,779-cycle acceptance requirement at
unchanged Fmax. Improving branch direction alone has still less headroom.
A fresh unchanged-core Gowin option-0 run reproduces 50.610 MHz and the
25.054 ns worst arrival path: register-file BRAM output through ID operand
selection, EX forwarding, a full-width DSP multiplier and ALU selection,
then the data-memory address port. This is a physical timed path even
though multiplication instructions do not perform data-memory accesses.
The canonical CoreMark ELF executes 93,960 MULs between the MMIO markers;
every one has the same low-32-bit result as a signed 16-by-16 product.
There are 35,640 immediate raw source dependencies after these MULs.
These observations favor computational value prediction over a larger
branch predictor: shorten the timed EX product path while preserving
single-cycle predicted-result forwarding for the common operand range.
A temporary prototype outside the core source tree was evaluated with the
unchanged harness. Gowin placement options 0/1/2 reached 52.548/54.014/
54.014 MHz, median 54.014 MHz. Stalled CoreMark retained exactly 4,201,709
counted cycles, all five canonical CRCs, the required validation literal,
and oob=false. The resulting projected fitness is 128.55, about 9.2 percent
above 117.75. Existing selftest and all three random-program cosim checks
passed both zero-wait and imem/dmem-stalled runs, with field-by-field ISS
comparison. This evidence is for a temporary prototype; the hypothesis
implementation must still pass unchanged formal and unit-test gates.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one stateless computational value predictor for multiplication.
In EX, use the fully forwarded operands to predict ALU_MUL as the 32-bit
signed product of a[15:0] and b[15:0], explicitly declared as two signed
16-bit inputs and a signed 32-bit output. This prediction deliberately
discards the upper operand bits; it is speculation, never an assumption
about legal RV32M operand values. Its result is exact when both operands
are sign-extended 16-bit values, including negative operands. For the
other multiply-family operations MULH/MULHU/MULHSU, predict zero initially
and use the same validation and recovery mechanism. The current workload
contains only MUL, but every legal high-product operation must remain
architecturally correct for arbitrary operands and instruction streams.
Do not add a result-history table, operand tags, a return predictor, or
another branch-prediction policy. Retain the existing bimodal/JAL logic.

Move full-width multiply evaluation onto the EX/MEM-to-MEM/WB path.
EX/MEM already carries the actual fully forwarded rs1_val, rs2_val,
operation, destination and instruction, so reuse those registered fields
as the exact multiplier inputs. Store the predicted product in its
alu_result field, making existing EX/MEM-to-EX forwarding deliver the
prediction to the immediately following instruction. In MEM, compute
the exact existing RV32M product variant from the registered operands,
compare it with the captured prediction, and always write the exact
product into MEM/WB. The retirement stage therefore commits the true
result and original operands even after an incorrect prediction.
Neither predicted values nor predictor correctness determine rvfi_trap.
Keep the full architectural 32-bit operands; do not narrow RVFI data.

On a mismatch for a valid multiplication that writes a nonzero rd,
generate an older-priority MEM repair to that multiplication's stored
PC+4. Preserve and retire the multiplication itself once with its exact
result. Flush the younger ID/EX instruction and current fetch, inject an
EX/MEM bubble instead of the younger EX result, and refetch the younger
instruction. Suppress that younger instruction's branch redirect,
direction-table training, divider start, and any other EX side effect
on the repair cycle. The younger instruction must never issue a memory
request, update architectural registers, or retire using a wrong product.
An older multiply's validation failure outranks every younger EX redirect
and frontend hazard. Skip recovery for rd=x0, whose speculative value
cannot be consumed. A correct prediction permits the younger instruction
to advance without a bubble; it continues to use the ordinary forwarding
priority. Use the registered EX/MEM pc_next for the repair target, which
is PC+4 for multiplication, to avoid an adder after the product comparator.

Keep the exact multiplier physically separated from EX's ordinary ALU
result selection. Add a constant ALU parameter, default enabled for the
standalone ALU tests, that disables its full-width multiplication cone
in the EX instance. This avoids relying on synthesis to eliminate a
full-width product hidden behind overlapping downstream opcode muxes.
Keep the standalone ALU's existing exact product expressions when that
parameter is enabled. Implement a local exact multiplier helper for MEM
using the same widths, signedness and four-product semantics. The EX instance
has only the narrow prediction for multiply-family results. Preserve
ADD/SUB/shifts, the shared iterative divider, all RV32M exceptions,
and the start/busy/result-valid/consume interface. This stage movement is
supporting machinery for validated value prediction, rather than a
separately interlocked multiplier redesign.

Under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS, both prediction and validation must use the
exact existing operation-specific add/sub-XOR formulas on the same
original operands. Keep all existing formal checks and bounds unchanged;
the ALTOPS configuration still exercises operand routing and normal
prediction acceptance. Directed real-arithmetic tests must also force
prediction failures, since narrow-product acceptance in CoreMark and
ALTOPS cannot validate the squash path. Do not modify any decoder legality
rule, the external ports, nret=1, RVFI order, memory contract, benchmarks,
or evaluation infrastructure. Keep load-use and bus/divider stall behavior
intact apart from the older-priority multiplication recovery signal.
On a MEM mismatch, suppress the younger EX divider-wait indication as
well as divider start, so the existing hazard unit's divider-hold priority
cannot defeat the older repair and leave wrong-path ID/EX metadata alive.

Expect 9 percent higher fitness, with medium confidence. All 93,960
profiled benchmark MUL predictions matched. The temporary prototype also
retained the exact counted cycle total and passed the canonical CRCs,
while raising median Gowin Fmax to 54.014 MHz. It used 3,385 LUTs and
947 FFs versus the champion's 3,000 LUTs and 841 FFs, with six DSPs
in both designs. The original DSP path ceased to be the worst path;
recovery/branch control and the remaining ordinary ALU paths became
limiting. These are preliminary prototype measurements, not a substitute
for implementation-phase formal, complete unit tests or repeated eval.
The gain comes from moving full-width validation behind registered
operands while preserving a narrow speculative product in EX. The risks
are a new MEM-product/comparison/recovery
critical path, extra DSP/register routing, and wide-operand recovery cost
on other workloads. Check actual DSP inference rather than assuming the
narrow expression maps well. Require unchanged formal and exact RV32M
tests, stalled CoreMark cosim and canonical CRCs, and median Gowin Fmax.
Acceptance requires (Fmax_new / 49.474 MHz) * (4,201,709 / cycles_new)
greater than 1.046. With unchanged cycles, median Fmax must exceed
51.750 MHz. Preserve every hard invariant and every existing test.

title: Isolate memory address generation from the general ALU result
motivation:
The champion scores 138.64 with median Gowin Fmax 58.252 MHz and
4,201,709 counted CoreMark cycles. Its recorded worst path is 23.440 ns,
from the register-file output through ID, EX and the ordinary ALU to a
data-memory address port. LESSONS.md is absent. The previous micro_opt
operand-preselection attempt raised Fmax but retained the general ALU
result path. Memory currently uses EX/MEM.alu_result for its address,
so every ALU result variant and operand-selection mux feeds the timed
memory-address circuit even though loads and stores only require rs1
plus a signed immediate. Separating this narrow function should remove
unrelated execution cones from the address path without costing cycles.

title: Register multiply repair and quarantine younger memory effects
motivation:
The champion scores 138.64 at median Fmax 58.252 MHz with 4,201,709
counted CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent. The structural history
shows that interlocking every multiply added 187,413 counted cycles and
failed to beat the champion despite reaching 58.572 MHz. Registering all
control-flow redirects also lost throughput. The current design avoids
those common-case delays with narrow EX products and exact MEM products,
but its full-width product comparison directly drives frontend flush,
EX squash, divider launch suppression and pipeline enables. Read-only
vendor timing experiments that isolated operand or address paths exposed
this remaining loop: EX/MEM opcode through full-width multiplication,
validation and pipeline control, with about 23.6 ns arrival. Registering
multiply repair specifically can break this control feedback without
adding a cycle to correctly predicted multiplies or ordinary branches.

hypothesis.hypothesis:

signal to a registered MEM/WB repair record. Keep the existing signed
16-by-16 EX prediction, all full-width exact product variants in MEM,

mismatch and its already registered pc_next alongside the true product
entering MEM/WB. Recovery in the following cycle uses only this repair
record; there must be no full-product/comparison-to-frontend path.

A delayed repair must quarantine the additional younger instruction
that has already reached EX/MEM. While registered repair is asserted,
gate both dmemREn and every dmemWEn lane off before any bus transaction,
replace that younger MEM/WB capture with a completely cleared bubble,
and suppress its generation of another repair. Simultaneously squash
younger EX, clear ID/EX, invalidate fetch and install the recorded
multiplication pc_next. The original multiply is already in MEM/WB and
must retire once with its exact result and original operands. Preserve
its regfile write and RVFI order. Gate the hazard unit's memory-operation
qualification by the MEM quarantine signal, so a squashed younger load
or store and io_dmemReady=0 cannot hold up recovery. Actual surviving
memory transactions retain the established stable-request semantics.
Registered multiply repair has priority over every younger redirect,
load-use hazard and tentative divider wait, and fires exactly once.

A younger DIV/REM must not start on the cycle an older multiplication
is still undergoing unregistered MEM validation: a later repair could
otherwise leave a wrong-path divider busy. Export a metadata-only
validation-pending indication from EX/MEM for valid legal multiply
writers to nonzero rd and defer divider launch until that indication
has passed. The existing divider wait can retain the younger instruction
and drain MEM. Snapshot both fully forwarded operands when launch is
deferred, including values from an older WB writer that will disappear
on the next edge. If validation passes, launch with those captured
operands and retain the original source values for RVFI; if registered
repair fires, discard the deferred instruction and snapshots without
starting or resetting a surviving divider transaction. Do not gate a
started divider's arithmetic with this indication. This rare defer is
supporting machinery for the new recovery boundary, not a redesign of
multiply or divide arithmetic.

Clear repair and deferred-launch state on reset. An older multiplication
must not generate a repair while held or be retired again; a squashed
MEM multiplication must not create a second repair. Correct predictions
advance continuously with no quarantine, new interlock, or added cycle.

implementation_notes:
# Registered multiply repair and younger MEM quarantine

Implemented only in cores/bench RTL and test_*.py. The core remains nret=1
with unchanged top-level ports, arithmetic formulas, decoder, regfile,
ordinary branch recovery, and multiplication prediction policy.

Changes:

- MEM captures mismatch and the original multiplication pc_next in a
  one-cycle repair record when a legal nonzero-rd multiply advances with
  its exact result into MEM/WB. The product comparison now feeds only
  the repair register. Held multiplies do not generate repair records.
- Registered repair disables every younger MEM read/write request,
  replaces the entire younger MEM/WB payload with zero, and prevents a
  quarantined multiplication from generating another repair. The older
  exact multiply still writes its destination and retires once with its
  original RVFI operands and consecutive order.
- Core excludes quarantined MEM operations from hazard qualification.
  Repair therefore overrides irrelevant bus stalls, younger redirects,
  load-use hazards, and tentative divider waits.
- EX defers an unstarted DIV/REM during metadata-only MEM multiplication
  validation, saving both fully forwarded operands and the instruction
  payload in the existing divider payload register. Validation pass
  launches with that snapshot; repair discards it without starting or
  resetting the divider arithmetic. Started divider transactions keep
  running, including through stalls and validation indications.
- ALU has dedicated divider launch operand inputs. This small interface
  extension keeps deferred-operand selection out of ordinary ALU/address
  arithmetic; divider state transitions and all real/ALTOPS formulas are
  unchanged. Standalone ALU tests drive the added inputs.
- Extended pipeline/divider coverage and added test_mem_repair.py for
  registered timing, held validation, qualification, complete bubble
  clearing, all product variants, and reset. Pipeline cases cover every
  DIV/REM variant, loads/stores, all store widths, branches/JALR,
  consecutive mismatches, x0, disappearing WB sources, ready/stalled
  recovery, original operands, strict orders, finite progress, and
  bubble-free prediction matches. The predictor scoreboard still checks
  every actual training update; a branch that advanced during the prior
  validation cycle and is later quarantined is excluded only from the
  surviving once-per-retirement training sequence.

Local validation:

- Required Verilator lint: PASS, no warnings.
- Final complete unit suite: PASS, 14 pytest runners, including real and
  ALTOPS arithmetic, the expanded pipeline/divider coverage, and the new
  MEM repair checks.
- Local formal: PASS, 53 checks, 0 failures, on both the initial and final
  RTL implementations. No formal counterexamples or fix retries.
- NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench: PASS for selftest (with and without bus
  stalls) and stalled CoreMark CRC validation, rerun after the final RTL
  change.
- Stalled CoreMark: start=15053, stop=4216762; counted bracket remains
  exactly 4,201,709 cycles. Canonical seedcrc=e9f5, crclist=e714,
  crcmatrix=1fd7, crcstate=8e3a, crcfinal=fcaf; UART contains
  "Correct operation validated." No out-of-bounds accesses.
- Final vendor Gowin timing across placement options 0/1/2:
  50.815 / 53.304 / 53.304 MHz; median 53.304 MHz. Option 0 has 3512
  logic cells, 983 registers, 8 LUT-RAMs, 6 BSRAMs, and 6 DSPs. Its worst
  path arrives at 24.973 ns and crosses regfile/decode, EX control flow,
  fetch, and frontend redirect control. The full-product comparison is
  no longer on that frontend feedback path.
- Final scope check: no off-limits changes; git diff --check is clean.

The timing hypothesis is not accepted locally: with unchanged cycles,
the fitness ratio is 53.304/58.252 = approximately 0.9151, below the
required 1.046 (60.932 MHz). Correctness and throughput are preserved,
but placement exposes an existing control-flow/frontend path as limiting.
No unrelated prediction, address-generation, or global pipeline changes
were attempted to address that path. Formal-deep was not run; real
arithmetic is covered by the unchanged exact arithmetic unit suite and
cosimulation.

title: Predict the middle carry of EX arithmetic and validate full results in MEM
motivation:
The champion scores 138.64 at 58.252 MHz with 4,201,709 measured cycles.
Its remaining worst path passes through forwarded operands and u_ex/u_alu.
Round 3's validated narrow multiply prediction improved fitness by 17.74
percent, establishing an existing mechanism for retiring exact MEM results
while replaying younger consumers after a prediction failure. A profile of
the current stalled CoreMark run counted 909,731 ADD-family operations,
5,453 SUBs and 684,483 load/store address additions. Splitting addition at
bit 16 can shorten a frequently used execute cone without serializing
execution. The profile also found only 51,854 bimodal direction misses
and 13,735 JALRs; enlarging the branch table offers insufficient cycle
savings to justify this slot. Focus solely on computational carry prediction.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a stateless predictor for the carry or borrow entering bit 16 of
EX ADD/SUB. Compute the low 16 bits exactly. Compute the upper 16 bits
independently using a predicted carry/borrow, instead of propagating a
carry across the full 32-bit forwarded-operand path. For ADD, use the
carry out of the four-bit window a[15:12]+b[15:12]+seed. The seed is one
when either operand's low 12 bits are all ones and the other operand's
low 12 bits are nonzero, otherwise zero. This inexpensive special case
handles common decrement-by-one arithmetic without a full lower-half
carry chain. For SUB, predict a borrow when a[15:12] < b[15:12], assuming
no borrow into the window. Compute upper ADD as a[31:16]+b[31:16]+carry
and upper SUB as a[31:16]-b[31:16]-borrow, modulo 16 bits. Implement
each upper operation as one 17-bit two-operand chain: upper ADD is
bits [16:1] of {a[31:16],1'b1}+{b[31:16],carry}, and upper SUB is
bits [16:1] of {a[31:16],1'b0}-{b[31:16],borrow}. Avoid a three-operand
expression that can infer two serial 16-bit adders. These are fallible
predictions, not replacements for architectural arithmetic.

Put the predicted 32-bit result in EX/MEM so the ordinary forwarding
path can supply it to the immediately following instruction. Preserve
the original full-width forwarded rs1/rs2, PC, instruction and controls.
Also capture the already-selected full-width alu_a and alu_b and the
single predicted carry/borrow bit into EX/MEM. AUIPC's base is PC;
ADDI/load/store use their correctly sign-extended I/S immediate;
register ADD/SUB use rs2. Exact MEM arithmetic consumes those registered
operands directly; do not recreate immediate decode or operand muxes
ahead of MEM validation. A shared exact 32-bit add/sub datapath supplies
the architectural result. Correct only
ADD, ADDI, AUIPC, SUB and load/store address computations. JAL/JALR
retain their PC+4 link values even though their decoder's default ALU
operation is ADD. Branches, LUI, illegal instructions and unrelated
operations must not acquire arithmetic effects from that default.

Always select the exact MEM result for ordinary arithmetic writeback.
For valid non-load arithmetic writers with rd != x0, validate only the
carry/borrow bit. Obtain actual carry from bit 16 of a 17-bit unsigned
lower-half addition, or actual borrow from bit 16 of a 17-bit unsigned
lower-half subtraction. XOR it with the captured prediction bit.
Exact low halves and deterministic upper arithmetic make that one-bit
comparison sufficient; no full-result equality belongs in the recovery
control cone. On a mismatch, preserve and retire that older
instruction once with the exact result, then use the existing older
MEM repair path to its stored pc_next. Flush ID/EX and fetch, insert an
EX/MEM bubble, and replay younger instructions. Suppress younger EX
redirects, branch training, divider launch and divider-wait on that
edge, exactly as current multiply repair does. Correct predictions
retain ordinary forwarding and bubble-free advancement. Keep the
existing multiply predictor and exact validation; combine the two
mismatch causes into one older MEM recovery indication. Both causes
are gated by valid advancement and cannot retrigger while held.

A predicted effective address must never select the wrong memory word.
For every load/store, drive the full architectural address in MEM using
the exact arithmetic upper half and the EX/MEM-registered low 16 bits.
Those low bits are exact for both split addition and split subtraction;
retain them directly for bus address bits [15:0], byte masks, alignment
checks and load extraction. This preserves the registered low address
feeding the unchanged FPGA wrapper's memory, rather than putting a
fresh combinational lower-half adder on its RAM address. Stores need
no replay solely for an address-prediction error because the actual bus
address is corrected before the request. Loads keep the existing
load-use interlock and exact loaded-data WB path, and must not compare
their effective address prediction as if it were loaded register data.
Keep waiting memory requests stable and preserve all misalignment traps.

Make the prediction an elaboration-time option enabled only in the EX
ALU instance, with the standalone ALU default remaining exact. Remove
the full-width EX ADD/SUB result cone when prediction is enabled;
leaving a parallel exact adder in EX defeats the purpose. Keep shifts,
comparisons, branch/JAL/JALR target arithmetic, multiply behavior and
divider transactions intact. Use the same base-ISA prediction and exact
correction in normal and RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS builds; preserve all existing
M-extension ALTOPS formulas and do not hide ADD/SUB recovery from formal.
No top-level port, nret, decoder rule, retirement ordering, benchmark,
evaluation file or correctness check changes are proposed.

The expected gain comes from shortening EX carry propagation and moving
exact validation behind registered operands. Risks are added MEM
arithmetic/validation delay, routing pressure, and replay cycles
on unfavorable operand patterns. Validate forced carry and borrow misses
in directed tests, exact RV32IM retirement, bus stalls, canonical CoreMark
CRCs and median Gowin timing. Require
(Fmax_new / 58.252) * (4,201,709 / cycles_new) > 1.046.

title: Use a flop register file with word-local one-hot bypass reads
motivation:
The champion scores 138.64 at 58.252 MHz with 4,201,709 measured
CoreMark cycles. A fresh Gowin timing report confirms that its worst
path starts at a register-file BSRAM, whose clock-to-output delay is
2.260 ns, then crosses operand selection and the ALU before reaching
the timed memory interface. Earlier decode operand preselection
improved its then-parent but did not beat this champion; repeating it
on the current RTL also failed. A distributed-RAM register-file probe
removed the two register-file BSRAMs but reached only 57.741 MHz.
A flat one-hot flop register file instead reached 59.880 / 60.833 /
60.833 MHz across the three vendor placement options and passed all
five existing register-file tests. Its 4.43 percent frequency gain is
just below acceptance. This proposal refines that same register-file
read implementation by folding write-first bypass into word-local
selection, rather than adding another architectural feature.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Implement the existing 32x32 register file as resettable flops with
explicit one-hot asynchronous read selection. Apply Gowin's supported
syn_ramstyle="registers" attribute to the data array, preserving the
original synchronous all-zero reset and single nonzero-register write.
For each register i=1..31, form write_i = w_en && w_addr==i and two
read selects read1_i = rs1_addr==i and read2_i = rs2_addr==i. Share
write_i across both read ports. The stored-word contribution on port k
is regs[i] AND replicated(readk_i && !write_i). Thus a word being
written never contributes stale data, with suppression derived from
the local decoded write address rather than a high-fanout global
read/write match. Never include x0 in the stored-word reduction.

Form each read result as the OR of these masked words and a bypass
candidate w_data AND replicated(w_en && w_addr!=0 && w_addr==rsK_addr).
In a procedural reduction, initialize the accumulator to this bypass
candidate and then OR registers 1 through 31 in ascending order.
Exactly one stored word or the bypass candidate may contribute.
This removes the separate wide write-first mux after the register
array read while retaining exact same-cycle behavior on either or
both ports. Use ordinary synthesizable SystemVerilog, not FPGA
primitives, so formal and simulation see the same storage and masks.
Keep the complete existing reg_file interface and ID/EX boundary.

This is one local physical implementation change to register-file
reads. Keep instruction timing, forwarding priority, source snapshots,
multiply prediction and repair, divider transactions, branch handling,
memory handshakes, trap discipline, RVFI ordering and nret=1 unchanged.
The register file must remain zero after every reset, including a reset
coincident with an enabled write; subsequent combinational bypass must
retain the original module's behavior. In particular, reads of x0
always return zero, writes to x0 never alter storage, and both read
ports observe a completed write coherently.

The measured flat-selector probe is evidence for the physical storage
angle, not a claimed accepted improvement: 60.833 MHz alone misses
the 60.932 MHz threshold. The local bypass refinement is intended to
remove remaining read selection depth and routing pressure sufficiently
to exceed that threshold with the same 4,201,709 CoreMark cycles.
Principal risks are extra flop/LUT area and an exposed multiply-repair
or forwarding-control critical path. Confirm the actual mapped
resources and all three Gowin placement options. Keep every existing
correctness gate and require (Fmax_new/58.252)*(4201709/cycles_new)>1.046;
do not claim a win from eliminating BSRAMs or from unit tests alone.

title: Retime operand preparation and one-hot bypass decisions into ID
motivation:
The champion scores 138.64 at 58.252 MHz with 4,201,709 measured
CoreMark cycles. Its worst path starts at the inferred register file
and crosses ID, EX forwarding, operand selection and the ordinary
ALU before reaching memory. Prior structural redirect/repair retiming
did not remove this datapath limit, while serial multiplication lost
cycles. Round 3's operand preselection improved its starting champion
but was overtaken by narrow multiply prediction. No recorded attempt
retimed forwarding decisions together with operand preselection.
Moving operand preparation across the existing ID/EX boundary can
shorten EX without a new pipeline stage or extra dependency stalls.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion scores 138.64 at 58.252 MHz with 4,201,709 measured
CoreMark cycles. Its worst path starts at the inferred register file
and crosses ID, EX forwarding, operand selection and the ordinary
ALU before reaching memory. Prior structural redirect/repair retiming

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make one structural change to the ID/EX operand-delivery boundary:
prepare PC/immediate operands and resolve the next instruction's
bypass decisions in ID, then register both data and selections on
its normal capture edge. Keep the existing pipeline depth, issue
rate, register-file module and every instruction's architectural
latency. Preserve the champion's narrow multiply prediction with
exact MEM validation, branch prediction and iterative division.

Add alu_a_val and alu_b_val to id_ex_t. ID captures alu_a_val as
dec_is_auipc ? fetched_pc : rs1_data, and alu_b_val as dec_alu_src ?
decoded_imm : rs2_data, using the existing write-first RF outputs.
Hold and clear these fields with the rest of ID/EX. Retain the
original source values, addresses, PC and controls for architectural
forwarding, stores, branches, multiplication and RVFI.

Change forward_unit from live EX tag comparison to registered,
three-way one-hot selections aligned with ID/EX. For each currently
fetched source address, compare first against the current ID/EX
destination that will enter EX/MEM on this edge, then against the
current EX/MEM destination that will enter MEM/WB. Select bits are
001 for captured ID data, 010 for next EX/MEM data, and 100 for next
MEM/WB data. A matching nonzero near writer wins over a far writer;
x0 never forwards. Export qualified write indications from EX's
post-trap control and MEM's post-alignment-trap control, each gated
by its instruction validity. Do not qualify from raw decoder write
bits: a misaligned JAL/JALR or load must not become a bypass writer.
Sample selections only when ID/EX captures, retain them when ID/EX
stalls, and reset/flush them to 001 whenever ID/EX resets/flushes.
Selection flops may live in forward_unit with exactly the same
clock/reset/stall/flush conditions as ID, avoiding extra bundle fields.

In EX, replace each architectural rs1/rs2 priority mux with the OR
of three masked candidates: original ID value, EX/MEM result, WB
result. Use the corresponding registered one-hot bits directly.
For ALU A, allow the near/far masks only when !is_auipc; otherwise
select captured alu_a_val. For ALU B, allow the near/far masks only
when !alu_src; otherwise select captured alu_b_val. The base mask
is neither forwarding mask, so exactly one candidate contributes.
PC/immediate operands cannot be overwritten by coincidental raw
register-field matches. Feed the ordinary ALU and divider launch
from these prepared ALU operands. Branches, JALR, store data,
multiplication prediction and RVFI retain the fully forwarded
architectural source values.

Preserve all current hold, drain and recovery behavior. During a
dmem hold, ID/EX and its selections stay together and the existing
retained WB payload remains available even after WB valid clears.
On a load-use bubble, clear selections with ID/EX; when the dependent
instruction is subsequently captured, the load is the far writer
and its next-cycle WB load value is selected. Divider launch captures
operands once; completion forwards its result through EX/MEM without
another issue bubble. Older multiply repair clears younger selections
and payloads, suppresses younger divider launch/training/redirect,
and retires the exact older product once. Correct multiply predictions
preserve ordinary near forwarding. Keep all existing real arithmetic
and RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS formulas, decoder legality and alignment traps,
bus handshakes, top-level ports, nret=1 and consecutive RVFI orders.

An isolated implementation of this exact combined retiming completed
all unchanged Gowin placement options at 63.585, 65.936 and 65.936
MHz, median 65.936 MHz, 13.19 percent above 58.252 MHz. Option zero
used 3,777 logic cells, 970 registers, 40 LUT-RAMs, four BSRAMs and
six DSPs. The worst reported option-zero path now starts at a MEM
multiply operation tag, rather than the RF output. The proposed
source contains no explicit RF replacement or memory primitive;
changed operand capture lets Gowin infer distributed RF storage.
The isolated Verilator probe passed all 23 existing pipeline cases,
adapting only packed PC extraction for the added operand fields.
The unchanged run_coremark_ipc validator completed ten stalled
iterations with exactly 4,201,709 bracketed cycles, canonical CRCs,
the required UART validation literal and no out-of-bounds accesses.
Combining this measured throughput with median Fmax gives probe
fitness 156.93, approximately 13.19 percent above the champion.
Full formal was not run during hypothesis generation; implementation-
phase correctness and fitness gates remain authoritative. The expected
gain is thirteen percent with unchanged CoreMark cycles. Risks are
incorrect next-stage tag qualification, lost held WB forwarding,
and the remaining MEM multiplication-recovery path. Acceptance
requires (Fmax_new / 58.252) * (4,201,709 / cycles_new) > 1.046.

changes.description:

original architectural source values and all instruction metadata.
Put the new fields above existing fields if preserving old low-bit

Capture PC-versus-rs1 and immediate-versus-rs2 preselection into
alu_a_val/alu_b_val at the normal ID/EX edge. Apply exactly the
existing reset, flush and stall discipline to the new fields.

Compare fetched source addresses against the current advancing
EX and MEM destinations and their qualified write indications.
Register mutually exclusive 001/010/100 base/near/far masks for
each source, near writer taking priority. Match ID's reset/flush
and stall behavior and avoid all live EX-stage tag comparisons.

Consume registered one-hot source masks with parallel masked-OR

title: Narrow right-shift value prediction with exact MEM validation
motivation:
The champion reaches 138.64 fitness at 58.252 MHz and 4,201,709 counted
cycles. A fresh unchanged-core Gowin run reproduces the 23.440 ns worst
path from register-file bit 29 through forwarding and the EX ALU to
data-memory address bit 11. This downward bit dependence implicates
right shifting rather than carry propagation. The previous carry
predictor regressed to 130.99 and added 80,018 cycles. Branch direction
prediction already leaves only about 51,854 misses. A fresh architectural
profile finds 274,353 shifts, with 232,163 inputs sign-extended from
16 bits. This favors another computational value predictor that removes
the full-width right-shift cone from EX while preserving exact retirement.
LESSONS.md is absent; prior predictor attempts were reviewed in log.jsonl.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a stateless speculative right-shift result predictor, enabled only
in the EX ALU instance. For SRL, assume the input is zero-extended from
16 bits and predict zero-extended (a[15:0] >> shamt). For SRA, assume
it is sign-extended from 16 bits and predict the sign-extended arithmetic
right shift of signed a[15:0]. Declare a 16-bit intermediate explicitly
so synthesis cannot retain a 32-bit barrel shifter behind the narrowing.
Amounts 16 through 31 produce zero for SRL and the replicated narrow
sign bit for SRA. SLL and every unrelated operation remain exact.
The assumptions are predictions, never restrictions on legal operands.

Capture the actual selected 32-bit shift operand and five-bit amount
with the speculative result in EX/MEM. This includes immediate shifts
and forwarded register shift amounts. The existing EX/MEM forwarding
path delivers the prediction to the younger instruction. In MEM, compute
the exact RV32I SRL/SRA result from those registered operands and always
commit it to MEM/WB. Validate predicted versus exact results for valid
legal right shifts that write a nonzero destination. Reuse the existing
older MEM multiplication repair to retire the shift exactly once and
replay younger instructions on a mismatch. Correct predictions retain
normal advancement. A mismatch uses stored pc_next, squashes the younger
EX transfer, and suppresses younger branch redirects, predictor training,
divider launch and divider wait. Combine shift and multiplication repair
with the same oldest-instruction priority; gate it on MEM advancement
so held instructions cannot repair or retire repeatedly.

Remove the full-width SRL/SRA computation from predictive EX at
elaboration time, while retaining the default exact standalone ALU and
the full-width MEM helper. Preserve original forwarded RVFI sources,
exact shift amounts modulo 32, all trap rules, memory addressing, the
current multiplication prediction, divider protocol and ALTOPS formulas.
Prediction and validation for base-ISA shifts operate identically in
normal and ALTOPS builds. Keep nret=1 and every top-level port unchanged.

The expected benefit is a shorter EX shifter and less routing on its
high-bit-to-low-bit path. Operand-width failures add replay cycles, and
exact MEM shift selection may become limiting. Profile actual SRL/SRA
match rates separately before final implementation; all-shift narrowness
is evidence of an opportunity rather than a claimed prediction hit rate.
Validate forced failures followed by dependent ALU/memory/control/divider
instructions, bus holds, exact RVFI retirement, canonical CoreMark CRCs,
and median Gowin timing. Acceptance requires
(Fmax_new / 58.252) * (4,201,709 / cycles_new) > 1.046.

implementation_notes:
# Narrow right-shift value prediction with exact MEM validation

Implemented the hypothesis in cores/bench only. The default standalone ALU
remains exact. Its new default-disabled NARROW_RIGHT_SHIFT_ENABLED parameter
selects explicitly 16-bit SRL/SRA intermediates, with separate elaboration
arms for narrow and full-width right shifts. Only the EX instance enables
prediction. SLL, multiplication predictions, divider arithmetic/protocol,
ALTOPS formulas, decoder legality, top-level ports and nret=1 are preserved.

EX/MEM now captures the selected full-width ALU operand and selected five-bit
amount, including immediate shifts and forwarded register amounts. MEM
always selects the exact registered-operand right shift for architectural
writeback. A legal, valid, advancing nonzero writer whose prediction differs
repairs through the existing older-MEM path shared with multiplication.
Stored pc_next supplies the replay address. This squashes younger EX effects,
redirects, branch training, divider launch and divider wait. MEM advancement
gates repair so a held payload cannot repair or retire repeatedly.

## Actual architectural profile, collected before implementation

The Python RV32IM reference executed the canonical 2K, -O3, ten-iteration
CoreMark ELF. These are actual result comparisons, rather than operand-width
proxies. All profiled right shifts wrote nonzero destinations.

| Operation | Whole-program shifts | Matches | Match rate | Bracketed shifts | Bracketed matches | Bracketed match rate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| SRL/SRLI | 80,789 | 67,232 | 83.2193% | 80,053 | 66,908 | 83.5796% |
| SRA/SRAI | 77,168 | 52,422 | 67.9323% | 77,086 | 52,346 | 67.9060% |

There are 37,885 predicted mismatches within the timing markers. Some wide
operands still produce matching results, especially for large arithmetic
shift amounts; signed-16-bit narrowness alone is not the prediction rate.

## Deviations and implementation concerns

- Squash and divider-wait bubbles clear validity, all effect/forwarding
  controls, and rd, while allowing unused data fields to capture the current
  execution payload. Reset and invalid input still clear the entire payload;
  downstream holds retain it. This removes late repair from the EX data mux
  and memory-address path. The original all-fields-zero bubble implementation
  measured only 52.901 MHz median. The divider-stage test now checks the new
  packed fields, disabled bubble effects, and exact held payload stability.
- MEM compares shift and multiplication predictions on separate operation
  paths before combining repair, avoiding comparison through the writeback
  result mux. Both retain the same oldest-instruction priority.
- Independent bus-hold assignments were separated in hazard_unit, and shamt
  was moved out of the ALU result block, to expose their actual dependencies
  and avoid false combinational-cycle warnings in public-flat cocotb builds.
- A new test_shift_mem.py directly verifies held MEM payloads, exact results,
  original RVFI source fields, invalid/illegal/nonwriting/x0 qualification,
  and no repeated repair after consumption, in real and ALTOPS builds.
- The exhaustive tests caught unsigned conditional-expression propagation in
  the first narrow arithmetic shifter. Both conditional arms are now signed.
  Yosys elaboration confirms the predictive ALU's $shr and $sshr operand
  widths are exactly 16; no 32-bit right-shift cells remain in that instance.
- Additional EX mux and shared-MEM-shifter simplifications regressed vendor
  timing and were reverted. The final RTL retains the best measured version.

## Local validation

- Required Verilator -Wall lint: PASS, no warnings. ALTOPS lint also passes
  with the existing intentionally unused FULL_MUL_ENABLED parameter ignored.
- Full cocotb suite: PASS, 18 pytest runners, including default and predictive
  ALUs in both arithmetic modes. New pipeline tests cover all 32 amounts,
  16-bit sign boundaries, wide inputs, SRL/SRA/SRLI/SRAI, forwarded amounts,
  x0, exact RVFI sources/results/order, bubble-free matches, dependent ALU,
  load/store/branch/JALR/DIV/REM consumers, bus holds and older repair priority.
- Local formal: PASS, 53 passed and zero failed on the final RTL. Both
  preceding complete runs also passed all 53 checks. No formal counterexample
  occurred and no formal-driven fix attempts were needed.
- NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench: PASS for all five ELFs, including selftest
  and random programs with/without bus stalls, plus stalled CoreMark CRCs.
  Canonical CRCs were e9f5/e714/1fd7/8e3a/fcaf, UART reported "Correct operation
  validated.", and no out-of-bounds access occurred.

## Final vendor timing and acceptance

Gowin placement options 0/1/2 measured 59.447/59.885/59.885 MHz; median Fmax
is 59.885 MHz. Area is 3,629 logic cells, 1,023 registers, eight LUT-RAMs,
six BSRAMs and six DSPs. The worst median-placement path now passes through
the existing narrow multiplication predictor rather than a full-width EX
right shifter; the worst reported arrival is 21.993 ns.

Stalled CoreMark start/stop cycles are 15,885 and 4,291,364. Only their
difference, 4,275,479 cycles, counts. This is 73,770 cycles above the champion.

Acceptance ratio = (59.885 / 58.252) * (4,201,709 / 4,275,479)
                 = 1.01029547.

This implementation is correct under the completed local checks but DOES NOT
meet the required ratio greater than 1.046. The approximately 1.03% fitness
increase is insufficient; do not classify this hypothesis as accepted.

title: Use operand-range certificates to shorten multiply recovery
motivation:
The champion scores 155.44 at median Fmax 65.311 MHz with 4,201,709
bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its 21.071 ns, 33-cell worst path starts in
MEM's exact multiplier and reaches younger EX and memory outputs through
the exact-versus-predicted product comparison and recovery. The existing
predictor already has a simple sufficient correctness condition: MUL is
exact when both original operands are sign-extended 16-bit values. That
condition can be checked without waiting for a DSP product. LESSONS.md
is absent; relevant micro_opt and multiplication attempts in log.jsonl
were reviewed. Registered recovery regressed, so shortening recovery's
combinational predicate while retaining its current cycle is preferable.
