hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace MEM's full-width exact-product-versus-predicted-product equality
on the recovery control path with a cheap, sufficient correctness
certificate derived from the original registered operands and operation.
This optimizes validation of the existing multiply predictor; it adds no
predictor, execution stage or delayed recovery. Keep the exact multiplier
unchanged and always send its true result to MEM/WB for architectural
writeback, whether the certificate succeeds or fails.

In real-arithmetic builds, certify any multiplication when either full
32-bit operand is zero. Otherwise, certify ALU_MUL only when each operand
has bits [31:16] equal to sixteen copies of its own bit 15. Under that
condition the original operands equal the signed 16-bit inputs used by
mul_predictor, so the low-32-bit prediction is exact. For MULH, MULHU and
MULHSU, whose existing prediction is zero, certify when both original
operands have upper 16 bits zero. Both are then nonnegative and their
product is below 2^32, so every high-product variant returns zero.
Use bitwise equality/reduction logic, not multiplication, subtraction,
a stored prediction table or a fallback exact-product comparison.

For an advancing valid legal multiplication writing a nonzero rd,
repair whenever the certificate is false, even if the predicted value
happens to equal the exact result. The certificate is sufficient, not
necessary: false negatives cause safe additional replays, never wrong
results. For example, MUL of 0x00010000 by 1 has an incorrect low-half
prediction and must replay; MUL of 0x00010000 by 0x00010000 has a matching
zero prediction but may conservatively replay. A zero operand is always
certified regardless of the other operand's width. Uncertified operands
remain fully supported; never trap, truncate architectural operands,
commit an unvalidated product, or assume a benchmark-specific range.

Keep all existing recovery qualification and priority: reset and MEM
holds suppress repair, invalid/illegal/nonwriting/x0 payloads do not
repair, and a repair uses the saved pc_next. The older multiplication
retires once with its exact product and original RVFI sources. On that
same cycle, squash younger EX, flush ID, redirect fetch and suppress
its divider launch/wait, branch redirect and predictor training exactly
as today. Correctly certified operations keep the existing latency and
near bypass. Leave register-file, operand forwarding, all pipeline data
clearing, branch prediction, decoder, bus handshakes and iterative divider
unchanged. Preserve nret=1, top-level ports and all hard invariants.

Under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS the existing predictor and exact multiplier
use identical operation-specific add/sub-XOR formulas on identical
original operands. Certify every multiply in that build, preserving
those formulas unchanged in both helpers and the standalone ALU.
Do not apply real signed-16-bit range assumptions to ALTOPS arithmetic.
Real-arithmetic tests must cover both true prediction failures and
unnecessary but safe replays, since the ordinary formal gate substitutes
multiplication and cannot prove the real certificate's arithmetic fact.

An isolated probe changing only mem_stage.sv's recovery predicate has
completed the unchanged Gowin placement options at 72.526, 72.022 and
72.022 MHz, median 72.022 MHz. Option zero uses 3,682 logic cells,
1,002 registers, 40 LUT-RAMs, four BSRAMs and six DSPs. Its worst timing
path now traverses the existing EX narrow multiplier instead of MEM's
exact product/comparison. The existing complete pipeline test runner
passes, including real product variants, dependencies, mismatches, bus
holds, x0 and strict RVFI ordering. Additional directed cases pass
for wide matching products that conservatively replay, signed 16-bit
boundaries, all high-product variants, zero operands and dependent
stores under randomized bus stalls. The unchanged run_coremark_ipc
validator passes ten stalled iterations with exactly 4,201,709 bracketed
cycles, all canonical CRCs, the required UART literal and no out-of-bounds
access. This combines to probe fitness 171.41, approximately 10.28 percent
above the champion, exceeding the 4.6 percent threshold. The standard
local formal suite also passes all 53 checks in ALTOPS mode. These are
probe results; implementation-phase correctness and fitness gates
remain authoritative. Other workloads can pay extra recovery cycles for wide
operands whose predictions nevertheless match. Acceptance requires
(Fmax_new / 65.311) * (4,201,709 / cycles_new) > 1.046; at unchanged cycles
median Fmax must exceed 68.316 MHz.

title: Register multiply recovery and cancel younger divider transactions
motivation:
The champion scores 155.44 at 65.311 MHz with 4,201,709 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent; structural attempts in
log.jsonl were reviewed. Its current 21.071 ns, 33-cell worst path
starts in exact MEM multiplication and crosses recovery control
into EX and the memory-side circuit. Registering multiply repair
in round 4 regressed on the earlier RF-to-branch-limited design.
Round 5 has since registered ID operand preparation and bypass
decisions and changed inferred RF storage to distributed RAM,
making that prior negative result worth rechecking on this substrate.
An isolated implementation on the supplied champion now reaches
71.344 MHz median without adding measured CoreMark cycles.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make one structural change: move multiplication mismatch recovery
from combinational MEM validation to a registered MEM/WB repair
record, with explicit cancellation of younger work. Compute and
commit the exact product on the existing MEM/WB edge. Capture a
repair bit only for an advancing valid legal MUL-family writer
with nonzero rd whose exact result differs from its prediction.
Capture its already registered pc_next as the replay target.
The probe clocks the target on every unheld, non-quarantined MEM
advance; only the repair bit qualifies its use, avoiding a late
product-comparison enable on the 32 target registers.
Drive repair and its target exclusively from these registers.
Product selection/comparison must have no combinational route
into fetch redirects, ID flush, EX squash or divider control.
Prediction policy, actual multiply arithmetic and successful-MUL
latency remain the champion's existing implementation.

In the following cycle the original multiplication is in MEM/WB
and retires exactly once with its exact result and source values.
Its registered repair must quarantine the younger instruction now
in MEM: force dmemREn and all dmemWEn lanes to zero, suppress its
bypass-writer indication, replace its MEM/WB capture with a cleared
invalid bubble, and prevent it from creating another repair record.
Exclude quarantined memory operations from the hazard unit's dmem
stall qualification so io_dmemReady=0 cannot delay recovery.
Simultaneously squash younger EX, clear ID/EX and its registered
bypass selections, invalidate fetch and install the recorded target.
Registered older repair wins over younger EX redirects, branch
training, load-use stalls and tentative divider waits. Clear the
repair pulse on this edge; held MEM instructions never create it.

Handle speculative DIV/REM with cancellation rather than the round-4
deferred-launch machinery. A younger division may launch while the
older multiplication is validating in MEM. If that multiplication
subsequently repairs, cancel the divider transaction synchronously
on the repair edge, returning its FSM to IDLE and withdrawing busy
and result-valid. Cancellation has priority over start, arithmetic
progress and consumption; suppress result transfer and payload
capture on the same repair. Stored arithmetic bits may remain, but
cannot be exposed as a valid result or attached to a later request.
Replaying the division must capture fresh fully forwarded operands.
The in-order topology guarantees that any outstanding divider on
this older-MUL repair cycle belongs to younger work: a surviving
older divider would have blocked that multiplication from reaching
MEM until its result was consumed. Preserve uncancelled divider
arithmetic, exceptional results, completion latency and result holding.
Use the same cancellation protocol in real and ALTOPS builds.

Correctly predicted multiplications and ordinary instructions gain
no new bubbles or interlocks. Actual mismatches pay one additional
recovery cycle and may start then cancel a younger divider once.
Keep the existing ID-prepared operands, one-hot bypass decisions,
RF implementation, load-use behavior, WB data retention on dmem
holds, branch prediction, arithmetic formulas, decoder legality,
traps, all top-level ports, nret=1 and consecutive RVFI orders.
No evaluation-contract file or another core is changed.

stall generator and constraints produced placement-option Fmax
68.218/71.344/71.344 MHz, median 71.344 MHz. Option zero used
3,768 logic cells, 1,003 registers, 40 LUT-RAMs, four BSRAMs and
six DSPs. The limiting path now crosses WB result selection and
ordinary EX arithmetic, rather than multiply validation recovery.
Unchanged run_coremark_ipc completed all ten stalled iterations
in exactly 4,201,709 bracketed cycles, with canonical CRCs, the
required UART validation literal and no out-of-bounds access.
Projected fitness is 169.80, approximately 9.24 percent above 155.44.

title: Certify narrow multiply predictions before full-product validation
motivation:
The champion scores 155.44 at 65.311 MHz and 4,201,709 counted CoreMark
cycles. Its worst reported path runs from u_mem/u_mul_exact through MEM
repair and EX to the data-memory address. The existing predictor already
computes a signed 16-by-16 product in EX, but its recovery decision waits
for the full-width MEM multiplier and a 32-bit result comparison. Prior
predictor history reports 93,960 matching CoreMark MUL predictions;
a fresh architectural profile confirms that this operand certificate
accepts all 93,960 bracketed MULs, with no false rejection or additional
replay inside the measured window. Certification can remove exact
multiplication from the recovery control cone.
Registering recovery previously regressed to 53.304 MHz, and carry and
shift prediction added replay cycles. LESSONS.md is absent; the relevant
predictor and registered-repair experiments in log.jsonl were reviewed.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace result-equality validation of the existing computational multiply
predictor with a conservative operand-class certificate. Keep its EX
prediction exactly as implemented: MUL predicts the signed product of
the low 16 bits, and MULH/MULHU/MULHSU predict zero. In MEM, certify MUL
when both original registered operands equal their own sign-extended
low 16 bits, or either full-width operand is zero. These are sufficient
algebraic conditions for the predicted low 32-bit product to be exact.
Implement the two sign-extension checks as independent upper-bit XOR
reductions against bit 15, not through any multiplier or result mux.
The zero cases are also sufficient for every high-product variant;
certify those variants only when either full-width operand is zero.

A legal advancing multiplication writing a nonzero destination repairs
whenever it is not certified, even if its prediction happens to equal
the exact product. False rejection costs replay but never correctness.
Certification must have no dependence on exact_product or alu_result.
Always compute the full RV32M product from EX/MEM's original full-width
forwarded operands and commit that exact result through MEM/WB, as the
champion already does. No approximate product becomes architectural.
Do not change the EX predictor, product widths, arithmetic latency,
multiplier implementation, forwarding masks, or direction predictor.
This hypothesis changes the acceptance policy of one value predictor.

Reuse the current same-cycle, older-MEM-priority recovery with no extra
stage or memory quarantine: redirect to the stored pc_next, preserve and
retire the older multiply exactly once, flush younger ID/EX and fetch,
and inject a side-effect-free EX/MEM bubble. Suppress younger EX branch
redirects, predictor training, divider start and divider wait exactly as
today. Qualify rejection with !reset, !hold_wb, valid, legal, reg_write,
and rd != x0. Waiting or invalid instructions cannot trigger recovery;
x0 needs none because no architectural consumer can use its prediction.
Keep the retained WB forwarding data and all bus/load-use hold behavior.

Preserve the exact ALTOPS formulas in both predictor and exact helper.
Use the same conservative operand certificate and rejection policy in
ALTOPS builds. Since the substitute prediction is already exact, these
are harmless extra replays and let symbolic wide operands exercise the
recovery control without changing any formal configuration or bounds.
Preserve nret=1, top-level ports, actual RVFI source values and results,
precise order, decoder legality, traps and every evaluation invariant.

A fresh profile used the unmodified RV32IM reference interpreter and
the canonical 2K, -O3, ten-iteration ELF built from unchanged sources.
All 93,960 bracketed MULs are certified, all predictions match, and no
high-product instructions execute between the markers. Across the whole
program there are 94,054 MULs, of which 94,048 are certified and match;
the remaining six are actual prediction misses. Ten unbracketed MULHU
instructions are uncertified; three have coincidentally correct zero
predictions and therefore acquire conservative replays outside the
measured window. These can shift the pseudo-random bus-stall phase, so
unchanged bracketed replay count is not a claim of identical measured
cycle counts. The reference completes 2,937,037 instructions with all
five canonical CRCs, the validation literal, and no out-of-bounds access.
A separate boundary/random arithmetic sanity check covers 88,784
operation/operand cases, including 18,133 certified cases, with no
incorrect certificate. These are architectural profiling and algebraic
checks, not RTL correctness or FPGA timing measurements.

Check real arithmetic with signed-16-bit boundary values,
wide nonzero operands, zero operands, and wide inputs whose low product
coincidentally matches. Directed recovery tests must distinguish
intentional false rejections from incorrect certificates, cover all
four multiply variants, and exercise dependent ALU/load/store/branch/
JALR/DIV instructions, bus holds, x0 and older-repair priority.

Expect a shorter repair path with no extra cycles on certified MULs.
The full MEM multiplier-to-WB path and EX's narrow multiplier can become
the next limits, and conservative wide-operand replays are the main
throughput risk. Validate unchanged formal and exact RV32M tests,
canonical stalled CoreMark CRCs and median Gowin Fmax. Acceptance needs
(Fmax_new / 65.311) * (4,201,709 / cycles_new) > 1.046; with unchanged
cycles, Fmax must exceed 68.315 MHz. This is an unmeasured hypothesis.

title: Isolate memory address generation after registered multiply recovery
motivation: The champion scores 178.53 at 75.013 MHz and 4,201,709 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its worst path starts at a MEM/WB value, crosses EX forwarding and the narrow multiply predictor, and ends at data memory. MEM currently uses the general EX/MEM alu_result as the data-bus address even though loads and stores only need rs1+imm. A dedicated address path removes multiply and general result selection from this memory-facing cone. LESSONS.md is absent; prior micro_opt entries and recent outcomes in experiments/log.jsonl were reviewed. The earlier r4s0 address specialization regressed because its newly exposed full-product recovery path still crossed MEM and EX combinationally. The present champion has registered that recovery, making this specific earlier limitation materially different.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a dedicated effective_addr field to the existing EX/MEM payload. In EX, compute it using one combinational adder on the fully forwarded architectural rs1 and decoded immediate. Capture rs1+imm directly, bypassing AUIPC/ALU-source selection, ALU operation selection, speculative multiplication selection, and jump-link selection. Do not gate this field with additional memory-op decode on its timed input path. Capture, hold, reset and squash it with the same instruction as the existing EX/MEM fields, without adding a pipeline stage or changing any instruction latency.

In MEM, use only this registered effective_addr for io_dmemAddr, byte-lane masks, load extraction, memory alignment checks, and aligned RVFI memory addresses. Keep alu_result for the ordinary result/near-bypass path and exact-product-versus-prediction validation. Keep the existing rs2 store-data path, load extension and writeback, registered multiply repair/quarantine, divider cancellation, and branch/jump behavior. A waiting active request must remain stable for any length of dmem stall. Inactive bus addresses may differ; every accepted memory transaction and architectural RVFI value must remain identical.

Retain the existing divider snapshot/consume mechanism, including the address field in its whole-payload capture as in the measured probe. Do not add unmeasured clock enables, strip divider payload bits, change the multiplier, or combine this hypothesis with writeback/forwarding refactors. Preserve real and ALTOPS arithmetic, decoder legality and trap suppression, prediction/training, near-over-far priority, x0, frontend recovery priority, nret=1, all top-level ports and every evaluation check. This is one local micro_opt: specialize an existing combinational function and its destination register field.

An isolated implementation of exactly this address specialization completed the unchanged Gowin placement options at 74.410, 79.208 and 79.208 MHz, giving a median 79.208 MHz, 5.59 percent above the champion. The existing complete pipeline, memory-repair and EX-divider runners pass after updating only packed-field layouts and standalone input addresses to match the added payload field. All architectural, exact-result, ordering, hold, recovery and cancellation assertions are retained.

The unchanged run_coremark_ipc validator completed all ten stalled iterations in exactly 4,201,709 bracketed cycles. All canonical CRCs, the required UART validation literal, timing markers and bounded-access checks passed. Combined with measured median Fmax this yields probe fitness 188.514, 5.59 percent above the champion and above the 186.74238 acceptance floor. title: Decouple fetch with an eight-entry queue and registered capacity
motivation: The champion scores 178.53 at 75.013 MHz and 4,201,709 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its fetch PC advances only when ID/EX captures an instruction; load-use bubbles, data-memory waits and divider waits therefore waste otherwise ready instruction-bus cycles. With approximately 22 percent independent stalls on both buses, buffering complete fetched instructions can overlap those waits. LESSONS.md is absent. The structural history includes successful operand/bypass retiming and registered multiply recovery, while an earlier registered-redirect experiment lost throughput. Isolated probes in this hypothesis-generation session found that moving multiplication to MEM alone and retiming the WB result mux do not exceed the current fitness threshold. The proposed single structural angle is frontend/backend decoupling; the existing execution and prediction datapaths remain the champion's.

hypothesis.motivation: The champion scores 178.53 at 75.013 MHz and 4,201,709 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its fetch PC advances only when ID/EX captures an instruction; load-use bubbles, data-memory waits and divider waits therefore waste otherwise ready instruction-bus cycles. With approximately 22 percent independent stalls on both buses, buffering complete fetched instructions can overlap those waits. LESSONS.md is absent. The structural history includes successful operand/bypass retiming and registered multiply recovery, while an earlier registered-redirect experiment lost throughput. Isolated probes in this hypothesis-generation session found that moving multiplication to MEM alone and retiming the WB result mux do not exceed the current fitness threshold. The proposed single structural angle is frontend/backend decoupling; the existing execution and prediction datapaths remain the champion's.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Insert an eight-entry elastic instruction FIFO between the existing fetch predictor/PC and decode. Each entry holds the full instruction, its fetch PC and the exact predicted_taken bit used to advance the fetch PC. Fetch accepts io_imemData and advances the predicted PC whenever io_imemReady is high, the FIFO has capacity, and no redirect is being applied, independently of load-use, dmem and divider holds in the backend. Decode consumes only the oldest queued entry when ID/EX can advance without a flush. Independent fetch and consume events can occur on the same edge. This keeps one instruction issue and one retirement per cycle while buffering bus availability across backend stalls.

Implement an eight-slot circular queue with three-bit head/tail pointers and a four-bit occupancy count. Only occupied entries or a ready empty pass-through instruction are valid; full queues never overwrite live entries. Drive fetch space exclusively from registered occupancy < 8; do not feed dequeue or redirect combinationally into this capacity signal. A full queue may dequeue, but cannot accept a replacement until the following cycle shows space. When occupancy is between one and seven, simultaneous enqueue/dequeue advances both pointers and leaves count unchanged. This intentionally breaks the backend-to-fetch ready path at registered occupancy. Reset and redirect clear count and pointers with priority over enqueue/dequeue. Payload bits need not reset, but stored payload cannot produce a valid instruction after the clearing edge; no unknown bits may reach a valid retirement. Use an empty-queue pass-through: when count is zero, present the current fetch bundle to decode with validity qualified by io_imemReady. A ready instruction can be enqueued and dequeued on the same edge without becoming a live buffered entry; if decode cannot accept it, enqueue it and retain it at the head. For a nonempty queue, decode always sees the oldest stored instruction, independently of bus readiness. Implement stored payloads as flat packed bit vectors, not arrays of typedef structs: a preliminary Yosys formal probe of the latter representation discarded the payload. Preserve the complete bundle bits with explicit pack/unpack assignments and require the cover check to reach a valid nontrapping retirement.

The fetch predictor remains in if_stage and sees the current bus instruction and fetch PC. Its accept now means successful FIFO enqueue, so a held or unready fetch cannot consume prediction or change PC. On enqueue preserve exactly that prediction with its PC and instruction. Decode, register-file read addresses, registered bypass preparation and load-use comparisons must all use the FIFO head instruction, never the unrelated current io_imemData. Qualify the hazard unit's instruction-available input with FIFO-head validity rather than io_imemReady, allowing already buffered instructions to issue during an instruction-bus stall. Dequeue only when head-valid, !stall_id and !flush_id; a load-use bubble keeps the head queued, and a downstream hold retains both the ID/EX instruction and the next queue head.

Keep current EX branch/JALR resolution, training, narrow multiply prediction, exact MEM validation, registered older multiply repair, divider cancellation, memory semantics and WB boundary. Every redirect, including older registered MUL repair, atomically discards all queued younger instructions and sets the fetch PC to the existing redirect target, with priority over fetch acceptance and consume. Suppress enqueue during redirect and rely on the existing highest-priority ID flush to prevent a younger capture. Present head validity from occupancy or raw-ready empty pass-through only, without a combinational !redirect term. On the redirect edge, clear FIFO metadata and ID/EX together. Keep redirect gating on fetch enqueue, but do not propagate it into the FIFO data/valid lookup or capacity network. The original redirecting instruction still advances and retires once. Correct branch/JAL predictions need no queue flush. Prediction training remains gated by actual EX advancement, and each queued instruction retains the direction actually consumed at its enqueue edge even if the predictor table later changes. Branches already in the queue are recovered by the existing predicted-versus-actual comparison. Outstanding divider cancellation and younger MEM quarantine retain the champion's older-repair priority.

Empty-queue pass-through preserves current refill latency after redirects. Nonempty queued predictions can use older counter state; measure that cost against saved bus stalls. Preserve the entire top-level I/O and nret=1 contract, decoder legality defaults, all real and ALTOPS arithmetic, memory alignment traps, original RVFI operands, correct next PCs and consecutive retirement orders. Do not alter stall generators, benchmark sources, timing wrappers, formal bounds or any evaluator. This is a structural fetch scheduling change, with no cache, new prediction policy or execution-arithmetic optimization.

Validate FIFO empty/full/wraparound, simultaneous enqueue/dequeue, reset and redirect under each occupancy. Pipeline tests must distinguish fetch acceptance from decode acceptance, track fetched prediction metadata through queue holds and wraparound, and check no drop, duplicate, reorder or wrong-path side effect. Cover dmem holds, load-use, independent imem stalls, divider waits, both branch directions, JAL/JALR, older multiply recovery and canceled younger divides. Retain all architectural assertions and exact arithmetic checks. Assess unchanged formal, ready/stalled full-trace cosim, canonical stalled CoreMark CRCs and bracketed cycles, and all three vendor Gowin placement options. Acceptance requires (Fmax_new / 75.013) * (4,201,709 / cycles_new) > 1.046. The expected gain is six percent with low confidence; the main risks are FIFO mux/occupancy logic lowering Fmax and recovery/refill costs erasing the saved stalls.

An isolated eight-entry empty-pass-through probe with flat payload storage passed all eight ready/stalled selftest and random-program full-trace comparisons against the unchanged ISS. Unchanged run_coremark_ipc completed ten iterations in 3,975,958 bracketed cycles, 5.37 percent fewer than 4,201,709, with all canonical CRCs, the required validation literal and no out-of-bounds accesses. However, the preliminary queue returned capacity combinationally from dequeue and masked head validity with redirect. Its median vendor Fmax was only 67.487 MHz; a reported 20-cell path ran from WB result selection through EX recovery into ID forwarding selection. That preliminary circuit is a regression, not acceptance evidence. This final hypothesis removes those two queue-control feedback paths using registered capacity and ID's existing flush priority. That refinement has not been timed or fully proven. At the measured cycle count, acceptance needs median Fmax above approximately 74.244 MHz. Early unchanged formal checks passed causal, backward PC, illegal, unique and liveness properties on the preliminary flat-storage probe; complete formal and the cover check remain required implementation-phase gates. No formal result from the earlier packed-struct-array probe counts as a pass: it failed reachability because Yosys discarded the payload.

changes.description: Add an eight-entry elastic circular FIFO carrying full if_id_t payloads as flat packed bits. Use three-bit head/tail pointers, four-bit registered occupancy, and fetch-space = count < 8 with no pop/redirect combinational feedback. Allow empty pass-through qualified by raw bus readiness and simultaneous enqueue/dequeue when not full. A full dequeue frees capacity on the next cycle. Head validity depends only on occupancy or raw readiness; existing ID flush prevents redirect-cycle capture while FIFO pointers/count clear synchronously. Preserve all packed payload bits, ordering, capacity and prediction/PC pairing.

Separate raw fetch_w from queued if_id_w. Drive fetch acceptance from io_imemReady and FIFO capacity; connect decode and register-file preparation to FIFO head. Consume on head-valid and advancing nonflushed ID. Flush the complete FIFO on existing redirect, including registered older MUL repair. Use presented-head instruction fields for load-use and presented validity for backend instruction availability; empty pass-through requires raw bus readiness while stored heads do not. Keep all external ports, execution wiring, recovery priority and retirement unchanged. Keep FIFO head validity independent of redirect; flush_id clears ID/EX before any capture, while redirect synchronously clears the FIFO and suppresses enqueue. Do not add dequeue-to-fetch-space combinational feedback.

Clarify and enforce accept as FIFO enqueue rather than ID/EX capture. Preserve current instruction-qualified predictor, training and target logic; redirect overrides enqueue and all PC holds. Raw fetched bundle carries the exact PC/instruction/direction for enqueue, while backend holds no longer prevent a ready fetch with available space.

Treat frontend availability as queued-head valid rather than raw bus readiness. Preserve load-use bubble and downstream hold semantics using queued source fields, and existing redirect/divider/dmem priority. Empty queue advances an invalid ID payload while older instructions drain. Do not let io_imemReady invalidate a buffered head.

title: Use a native 9-bit multiply predictor with exact registered recovery
motivation:
The champion scores 178.53 at 75.013 MHz and 4,201,709 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path now traverses EX's signed
16-by-16 multiply predictor. Earlier carry and shift prediction added
replay cycles and lost fitness, while operand certification left this
multiply path limiting. Registered exact-product recovery is already
present, so a smaller speculative product can trade a modest increase
in replays for a shorter FPGA multiplier path without changing the
architectural arithmetic or adding another prediction mechanism.
LESSONS.md is absent; prior predictor attempts in log.jsonl were read.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace only the real-arithmetic EX MUL prediction with the signed
product of the low nine bits of each fully forwarded operand. Declare
two signed nine-bit inputs and an eighteen-bit signed product, then
sign-extend that product to 32 bits. The intended implementation uses
the FPGA's native 9-by-9 multiplier mode instead of the current
16-by-16 expression. Verify actual vendor inference; a smaller source
expression alone is not evidence of a shorter circuit. Keep zero
predictions for MULH, MULHU and MULHSU. Keep all ALTOPS formulas exactly
as today, using the original full-width operands in that build.

Keep MEM's full-width exact products, result-equality validation and
registered MEM/WB repair unchanged. Every multiplication commits its
exact RV32M result. A mismatch for a legal nonzero destination retires
the multiply once and uses the existing older-priority replay,
quarantining younger memory work and cancelling younger divisions.
Narrow operand ranges are predictions, never legality assumptions,
trap conditions, or restrictions on architectural source values.
Preserve original RVFI operands, successful-prediction latency,
forwarding, bus handshakes, decoder legality, nret=1 and every port.
Do not combine this with a certificate policy, branch predictor change,
new interlock, delayed validation, or exact-multiplier redesign.

An architectural profile of the unchanged canonical 2K, -O3,
ten-iteration program executed 2,937,037 instructions with no
out-of-bounds access and the canonical CRCs. There were 93,960 MULs
between the timing markers. The current signed-16-bit prediction
matches all of them; signed-nine-bit prediction matches 71,700 and
misses 22,260. This is an ISS operand profile, not an RTL cycle or
timing measurement. The additional misses must be included in the
stalled CoreMark cycle count. A nominal three extra cycles per miss
adds 66,780 cycles, about 1.59 percent; actual replay and bus-stall
overlap must be measured. A materially faster native narrow DSP path
could exceed the 4.6 percent acceptance threshold after that cost.

Validate exact arithmetic and forced speculative failures for all
multiply variants, both forwarding sources, signed-nine-bit endpoints,
values immediately outside that range, and arbitrary full-width
operands. Directed pipeline checks must cover dependent ALU, load,
store, branch, JALR and DIV/REM instructions, consecutive misses,
x0, held operands, older repair priority and cancellation. Preserve
every existing architectural assertion and recovery check; update only
assertions tied to the predictor's former signed-16-bit policy.
Run unchanged formal, canonical stalled CoreMark validation and median
Gowin timing. Acceptance requires
(Fmax_new / 75.013) * (4,201,709 / cycles_new) > 1.046.
DSP mapping, extra replays and another path becoming critical are the
principal performance risks. This remains an unmeasured RTL hypothesis.

title: Remove redundant outcome qualification from predictor training data
motivation: The champion scores 188.51 at 79.208 MHz with 4,201,709 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its 18.733 ns worst path starts at MEM/WB load data and traverses WB forwarding and EX branch resolution into the IF direction table. The training data is actual_taken, which repeats validity, branch-kind, legality and misalignment qualification already enforced by branch_train_en. This puts extra logic and shared recovery fanout after the late comparator. LESSONS.md is absent; the prior micro_opt attempts and recent outcomes were reviewed. Larger local rewrites exposed other critical paths without exceeding the acceptance threshold; a minimal exact data-path factorization is preferable here.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Drive branch_train_taken directly from branch_cond instead of actual_taken. Keep branch_train_en and the complete direction-table update logic unchanged. The existing training enable requires a valid advancing legal conditional branch, an aligned branch target, no downstream stall, no older multiply repair, and no divider wait. Whenever that enable is true, branch_taken equals branch_cond and misalign_fault is false, so actual_taken equals branch_cond. When enable is false, the table performs no update and the value of training data has no effect. This is an exact don't-care optimization of an internal qualified data signal, not a weaker validation or a new prediction policy.

Preserve actual_taken for redirects and every other existing consumer. Preserve branch_cond's signed/unsigned comparisons and reserved defaults, branch_taken qualification, jump/branch alignment traps, predictor indexing/reset/saturation and update edge, fetch acceptance, older repair priority and all RVFI values. Do not remove any gate from branch_train_en or alter target, redirect, squash or memory logic. No added state, stage, queue, replay, or policy change is needed. Keep nret=1, top-level ports, decoder legality defaults, exact and ALTOPS arithmetic, divider transactions and memory handshakes unchanged.

The intended benefit is to send the comparator's result directly to the counter update without routing it through branch_taken and recovery/alignment qualification. That removes serial logic and isolates counter data from recovery fanout while leaving the qualifying enable intact. Expect a six percent gain in Fmax and fitness with identical 4,201,709 measured CoreMark cycles. At unchanged cycles acceptance requires median Fmax above 82.852 MHz and fitness above 197.18146. The main risks are vendor optimization already recognizing the qualification redundancy and another execute or writeback path limiting the gain.

Retain all pipeline scoreboard and architectural checks. For every enabled event require the new training data to equal the original architectural branch outcome; disabled events must leave the table unchanged regardless of comparator value. Exercise all branch conditions, aligned and misaligned targets, legal/reserved instructions, stalls, older multiply repair, x0, and near/far forwarding including retained WB load data. Verify the predictor's complete sequence of counter updates, predictions, accepted fetch PCs and retirement order remains unchanged. Run unchanged formal, stalled cosimulation, canonical CoreMark validation and all three Gowin placements before claiming improvement.

title: Split operand collection from execution with an EX-result return bypass
motivation:
The champion scores 188.51 at median 79.208 MHz and 4,201,709 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent. Structural history favors register
boundaries: ID operand/bypass retiming and registered multiply recovery
won, while the eight-entry fetch queue and the early registered-redirect
experiment lost fitness. A fresh vendor placement-option-1 build
reproduces 79.208 MHz. Its worst paths include registered forwarding
selectors through branch resolution into predictor counters, and the
WB result mux through EX forwarding and the narrow multiplier into
EX/MEM. Moving only predictor training, flattening the WB bypass into
typed lanes, and replicating branch comparators did not improve vendor
timing in isolated probes. A registered control-flow probe passed all
eight ready/stalled trace comparisons and canonical CoreMark validation,
but cost only 1.52 percent more bracketed cycles with today's predictor.
The most promising remaining structural angle is a real operand/
execution pipeline boundary, which cuts forwarding off both arithmetic
and branch-resolution inputs while preserving dependent ALU throughput.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Split the current EX into an operand-collection stage OC and a registered-
operand execute stage EX: fetch/decode -> OC -> EX -> MEM -> WB. Keep the
existing ID/EX decoded instruction register as OC's input. Add one
OC/EX register holding fully resolved architectural rs1/rs2 values,
selected ALU operands, PC, immediate, instruction, destination, control
and the exact accepted predicted_taken bit. EX consumes these registers
directly: no current WB-result mux or forwarding selection may precede
its ALU, narrow multiplier, branch comparator, JALR adder or effective-
address adder. Keep EX/MEM, MEM/WB and the sole retirement boundary.
This is one structural pipeline split, not a cache, predictor-policy
change, arithmetic approximation or additional retirement channel.

Preserve one-per-cycle issue for dependent ordinary ALU instructions
with a same-cycle EX-result-to-OC return bypass. EX computes from stable
OC/EX operands; its correctly qualified current result can be captured
into the following instruction's OC/EX operands on the same edge that
the producer enters EX/MEM. Forward the architectural link for JAL/JALR
and the existing narrow MUL prediction where applicable. This result
feeds only OC operand collection, never current EX arithmetic: there
must be no combinational EX-result-to-EX-input loop or two ALUs in
series. The competing paths become registered EX operands -> operation
-> OC capture mux, and older registered results -> OC capture mux.
Independent instructions can advance OC and EX simultaneously.

Resolve OC dependencies against the nearest older writer first:
current EX, then current MEM, then WB, then the ID-captured source.
A matching but unavailable nearest producer blocks that source; never
fall through to an older writer of the same register. Gate producer
eligibility by valid, nonzero rd and final write qualification after
applicable target/access traps. Keep AUIPC's PC and immediate operand
selection distinct from architectural source values used for RVFI.
Repurpose forwarding logic for this new stage relationship instead of
retaining the old three-bit selections whose stage timing has changed.

Provide a MEM-result-to-OC bypass for aligned accepted loads using the
existing sign/zero-extended load result. A load in EX cannot forward its
address as data. Its immediate consumer waits in OC for one bubble,
then captures the accepted MEM load value into OC/EX. Thus the new
register does not inherently add a second load-use bubble. Qualify this
bypass with the real bus handshake and trap/write eligibility; an
unready or trapping load cannot produce a value. Resolve stores,
branches, JALR and multiply/divide operands by the same age rules.
Keep exact MEM multiplication and registered repair unchanged. A MUL
in MEM forwards its registered EX/MEM predicted product, with the same
recovery discipline as the champion; its exact product becomes a
bypass source only after the existing MEM/WB validation edge. Never
route the full-width combinational MEM multiplier into OC capture.
Current EX retains the champion's speculative narrow product.

Give OC explicit operand-ready state. During a hold, capture a resolved
source or matching older writeback before its forwarding slot drains,
and retain it while another source waits for a load/divider. Unresolved
nearest-producer tags must remain authoritative until that producer
completes or is found not to write. Do not let a long divider wait lose
an unrelated WB source or replace a pending youngest value with an
older one. Captured operands and prediction metadata stay paired with
the held instruction. Do not send an instruction into EX until its
required source values are ready; preserve original architectural
source values in the RVFI payload. Actual dmem backpressure holds the
pending MEM request and prevents EX overwriting EX/MEM. Occupied EX
must backpressure OC without dropping, duplicating or reordering work.

Resolve and train branches in EX from registered operands, using the
existing predictor and advancement qualification. Correct predictions
and direct JALs incur no new recovery bubble. A conditional misprediction
or JALR discards both younger OC work and the fetched/decoded instruction
while the resolving EX instruction advances and retires normally.
Clear the next OC/EX valid bit on that edge; do not squash the resolving
branch itself. An older registered MUL repair retains priority over
this EX redirect, quarantines younger MEM effects as today, and now
invalidates OC/EX, OC and decode together. Suppress OC capture and every
younger divider launch on recovery. Cancel an already launched younger
divider on older repair and discard its held result/payload. Divider
operands are the new registered EX operands, requests start exactly
once, older MEM/WB work drains, and completion is consumed exactly once.
Maintain bounded ALTOPS completion and the identical real/ALTOPS formulas.

Preserve the full core I/O and nret=1 shape, default-illegal decoder,
SYSTEM policy, alignment traps, bounded memory accesses, all RVFI
metadata and strictly consecutive retirement orders. Keep all evaluator,
wrapper, benchmark, stall-generator and formal-depth files unchanged.
Existing architectural assertions must remain; adapt stage-layout and
timing-specific scoreboards to the extra OC/EX register, and extend
them to check resolved-source retention and recovery of both younger
stages. Exercise back-to-back dependent ALU chains at one issue per
ready cycle, nearest-writer priority, load-to-every-consumer-class,
long divider waits with an unrelated retiring WB source, bus holds,
exact MUL repair, canceled divides and all branch/jump/trap cases.

Run unchanged formal and ready/stalled full-trace cosim, canonical
CoreMark CRCs/validation literal/MMIO brackets, and all three vendor
Gowin placements. Acceptance requires
(Fmax_new / 79.208) * (4,201,709 / cycles_new) > 1.046.
With a five-percent cycle increase, median Fmax must exceed about
87.0 MHz; 92 MHz would yield about ten percent more fitness. These are
design targets, not measurements of this pipeline. Added registers,
EX-to-OC return routing, the MEM load bypass and later recovery can
erase the gain. The complete OC/EX split has not been implemented or
timed; the isolated smaller probes are not acceptance evidence.

title: Speculate next PC through EX and register exact control-flow validation
motivation: The champion scores 188.51 at median Gowin Fmax 79.208 MHz with 4,201,709 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its worst path runs from MEM/WB load data through forwarded EX branch comparison into the IF direction table (18.733 ns). Merely registering training exposed the remaining comparison-to-recovery fanout and measured only 77.719 MHz with unchanged cycles, so that limited version is not the final proposal. LESSONS.md is absent; prior predictor attempts and outcomes were inspected. Bimodal/JAL prediction previously improved fitness, while arithmetic carry/shift prediction, narrow multiply certification and nine-bit multiply prediction failed acceptance. The opportunity is to let the existing branch prediction carry execution past EX and validate control flow behind registered operands, removing forwarded comparisons from same-cycle frontend recovery.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Extend the current instruction-qualified next-PC prediction into one scheme with registered MEM validation. Retain the existing 64-entry two-bit conditional direction table, weakly-taken reset and exact immediate JAL prediction. Add a small eight-entry, direct-mapped, fully tagged last-target bank for legal JALR, indexed by fetch PC[4:2], storing PC[31:5], target[31:2] and valid. A qualified aligned-target hit supplies the predicted JALR next PC; a miss predicts PC+4. Reset valid bits; unknown invalid tag/target storage must never affect lookup. The validated decoder remains the authority for instruction legality. Do not add a return stack, history predictor, fetch queue or arithmetic speculation.

Carry the exact predicted successor accepted by fetch through IF/ID and ID/EX alongside the existing conditional predicted-taken bit. EX computes architectural source forwarding, direct targets, the JALR rs1+immediate target with bit zero cleared and PC+4 link values, but no branch/JALR redirect or predictor training depends on forwarded operand comparisons in EX. Capture original full-width source operands, the resolved target, predicted direction and predicted successor in EX/MEM. Reuse its pc_next as the predicted successor for JALR if convenient. For branches, target calculation is PC+immediate and prediction direction alone selects the provisional successor. Do not leave an unused generic EX redirect-target mux whose data still depends on branch_cond: tie absent EX redirects off and explicitly remove their timed comparison cone. JAL alignment is known from the immediate; preserve its current trap and link suppression.

In MEM resolve conditional branches exactly from the registered original operands. Effective taken means a legal condition-true branch with aligned target. Validate direction with effective-taken XOR captured predicted-taken. Validate JALR independently by comparing its captured prediction directly with the registered resolved JALR target; OR in its alignment fault. Do not compare JALR prediction with a generic resolved-next-PC mux: that mux also depends on branch comparison and would put two full-width validation cones in series. Use separate conditional and indirect checks, combining only their qualified one-bit mismatch outputs. Correctly predicted control transfers incur no bubble. All architectural RVFI next PCs are selected from exact resolution in MEM, never from speculation.

Register a control-flow repair bit and exact target at the existing MEM/WB boundary, combining it with the current registered multiplication repair as one oldest-instruction recovery record. Clock the target independently of the mismatch enable. The resolving older instruction retires exactly once. title: Flatten OC forwarding, saved operands and ALU selection into one mux
motivation:
The current champion achieves 203.36 fitness at 85.344 MHz with
4,196,601 measured CoreMark cycles. Its worst Gowin path is a 17.775 ns,
ten-cell path from data-memory RAM through MEM and OC forwarding to
OC/EX alu_b_val[29]. The new operand-collection stage removed forwarding
ahead of execution, but its capture path still selects a forwarded
source, then a retained source, then an immediate or PC. LESSONS.md is
absent. Prior micro_opt attempts show that local operand preselection
can help, while register-file replacement and branch-training gate
removal failed acceptance. Flattening the now-critical OC selection
offers a local timing improvement without adding load-use latency.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the serial OC source-forwarding, saved-source and ALU-operand
muxes with one mutually exclusive masked-OR candidate network per
destination. Keep the current ID/OC and OC/EX boundaries and every
instruction's advancement edge. Compute producer matches and readiness
with the current strict EX-over-MEM-over-WB-over-ID ordering. A matching
unavailable nearest producer must block capture and must never select
an older value. Readiness is control for capture, not another wide data
mux. Preserve all valid, trap, x0 and recovery producer qualification.

For each architectural source, derive disjoint selects for the saved
operand, current EX result, MEM bypass, WB result and ID snapshot. When
its existing rsK_ready_q is set, select only rsK_value_q and disable all
live producer and ID candidates. Otherwise use the current forwarding
winner, with all candidates disabled for x0. Express rsK_value as one
OR of the bitwise-masked candidates; remove the subsequent
rsK_ready_q ? rsK_value_q : forwarded_value mux. Reuse this flattened
result for architectural source capture and one-time source retention.

Independently form each ALU operand directly from the same candidate
data, without passing through the architectural source-result mux.
For operand A, gate every register/saved-source candidate with
!in.ctrl.is_auipc and add in.pc masked by in.ctrl.is_auipc. For operand
B, gate every register/saved-source candidate with !in.ctrl.alu_src
and add in.imm masked by in.ctrl.alu_src. Thus immediate and PC
selection are absorbed into the one-hot enables ahead of the wide
network. Keep architectural rs1/rs2 independent of ALU operand
selection, so stores, branches, JALR, multiplication and RVFI still
receive the exact resolved register values. Expose producer selects
from forward_unit or extend its internal interface as appropriate;
avoid reconstructing another priority data mux in operand_stage.

Preserve source retention while one operand is blocked or EX is held,
clearing saved-ready flags on exactly the existing advance/reset/flush
edges. Never refresh a saved operand from a later draining producer.
Keep full-rate EX-to-OC dependent ALU forwarding, accepted MEM loads
with the existing single load-use bubble, divider holding, memory
backpressure, multiply repair/quarantine, prediction and retirement
unchanged. Preserve nret=1 and all external ports and invariants.

The falsifiable prediction is identical bracketed CoreMark cycles
and an eight percent increase in median Fmax and fitness, from removing
two serial wide selections after the MEM return value. Acceptance at
unchanged cycles requires median Fmax above 89.269824 MHz and fitness
above 212.71456. Other MEM formatting or EX arithmetic paths and vendor
factoring of the explicit one-hot logic may cap the gain. Validate
with the existing OC/pipeline tests, unchanged formal and stalled
cosimulation/CoreMark CRC gates, then all three vendor placement
options; an area change or one favorable placement alone is not a win.

implementation_notes:
# Flatten OC forwarding, saved operands and ALU selection

Implemented the hypothesis in `cores/bench/rtl/forward_unit.sv` and
`cores/bench/rtl/operand_stage.sv`.

`forward_unit` now exports disjoint five-bit candidate enables ordered as
saved, EX, MEM, WB and ID. Saved-ready flags suppress all live candidates;
x0 disables every data candidate. Producer matches retain the original
qualified EX-over-MEM-over-WB-over-ID priority. An unavailable nearest
matching producer still blocks readiness and cannot expose an older value.
Readiness affects capture only, not the wide data enables.

OC forms each architectural source as a single masked OR of the saved
operand and four live candidates. This same result feeds OC/EX architectural
source capture and one-time retention. Separate ALU A/B masked-OR networks
read the candidates directly. Their scalar enables absorb AUIPC PC and
alu_src immediate selection, removing the saved/live and PC/immediate
wide muxes after forwarding.

The ID/OC and OC/EX boundaries, capture edges, retention reset/flush/advance
priority, producer qualifications, and external nret=1 interface are
preserved. No EX/MEM/WB arithmetic, prediction, memory, or retirement logic
was changed. The internal forwarding interface is now control-only; this
is the interface extension permitted by the hypothesis.

Existing assertions were retained. Added operand-stage tests cover both
sources resolving on different edges, saved operands overriding changing
EX/MEM/WB/ID candidates (including unavailable writers), hold release and
the following instruction, raw-source blocking despite PC/immediate
selection, and retained x0. Added pipeline tests cover a draining WB
operand while another source waits for a load or divider, subsequent
dependent ALU/store/branch/JALR instructions with independent bus stalls,
and multiply recovery clearing saved WB state before divider capture.
The existing architectural and advancement scoreboards remain intact.

Local validation:

- Required Verilator lint command: PASS, no warnings.
- Full cocotb suite: PASS (16 pytest runners). Final pipeline suite includes
  39 cocotb tests; operand-stage suite includes seven.
- Formal: PASS on the first run, 53 passed and 0 failed; no fix retries or
  counterexamples. Command: `CORE_NAME=bench RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl JOBS=8
  bash formal/run_all.sh` (automatically selects the unchanged nret=1 gates).
- Cosimulation: PASS, selftest RVFI checked with and without bus stalls,
  plus stalled CoreMark CRC validation. Command:
  `make cosim TARGET=bench NRET=1`. The initial invocation without NRET
  encountered the build script's nret=2 default; rerunning with the existing
  nret=1 contract resolved this without changing any harness files.
- `make timing TARGET=bench`: PASS, placement option 0 at 87.616 MHz.
- `make fpga TARGET=bench NRET=1`: PASS, all three vendor placements and
  stalled bracketed CoreMark completed.

Measured placement Fmax values: 87.616, 91.186 and 91.186 MHz.
Median Fmax: 91.186 MHz. Fitness: 217.29 iterations/second.
CoreMark: exactly 4,196,601 bracketed cycles for ten iterations, unchanged
from the champion. Both required thresholds are exceeded: 89.269824 MHz
and 212.71456 fitness. The measured improvement is about 6.85%, below the
full eight-percent prediction.

Area: 4,222 logic cells versus 4,025 previously (+197); 1,329 registers
unchanged; eight LUT-RAM, six BSRAM and six DSP. Option 0's worst setup path
is now 16.487 ns across nine cells from data RAM through MEM/OC into the
multiplier input register absorbed by synthesis, versus the reported
17.775 ns ten-cell baseline path. Other EX arithmetic/control and OC
retention paths remain close behind it. Placement option 0 alone misses
the acceptance threshold; the measured median across all three options
passes. The area increase and remaining critical paths are the main
implementation tradeoffs.

title: Unify retained sources and bypass routing in the OC capture crossbar
motivation:
The champion scores 203.36 at median Gowin Fmax 85.344 MHz with
4,196,601 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its successful OC/EX split leaves
a 17.775 ns worst path from data-memory RAM through MEM formatting,
OC forwarding and prepared-operand capture. The present capture topology
resolves a four-source forwarding mux, then selects a separately retained
operand, then selects PC/immediate for the ALU registers. This serial
topology also extends EX-result return paths. LESSONS.md is absent.
Relevant prior structural outcomes favor operand isolation over added
branch latency or fetch buffering. Local probes confirmed that delaying
load forwarding loses both cycles and Fmax, and moving a bank-selection
mux before EX arithmetic lowers Fmax substantially. The promising angle
is to restructure capture itself while preserving registered EX operands
and the champion's dependency schedule.

hypothesis.hypothesis:

crossbar inputs for prepared ALU roles. Build separate capture outputs
for architectural rs1, architectural rs2, ALU a and ALU b directly from
mutually exclusive control masks. The data path is candidate bus ->
mask/balanced OR -> existing OC/EX register. No output of a complete
forwarding mux may then pass through a retained-source mux or an
immediate/PC mux. No source-selection mux moves after OC/EX into EX.
This is one structural replacement of the operand-capture topology,
not an additional pipeline stage, arithmetic approximation or new
predictor/memory policy.

For each source, a saved-ready value has priority and suppresses every
live producer route; otherwise x0 selects zero, followed by the nearest
qualified EX writer, then MEM, then WB, then the ID snapshot. Qualify
every writer exactly as today: valid, nonzero destination and final
post-trap write eligibility, with older repair suppressing younger work.
Select producer identity independently of readiness. An unavailable
nearest EX load/divider or MEM load must block capture instead of
exposing an older same-rd value. Generate explicit mutually exclusive
one-hot masks, rather than an encoded route followed by another decoder.
For ALU a, AND all architectural route masks with !is_auipc and add
PC masked by is_auipc as a parallel term. For ALU b, AND source masks
with !alu_src and add immediate masked by alu_src. Architectural RVFI
source capture remains independent of these ALU operand roles.

occupied-EX hold and flush priorities. The ordinary resolved-source
path may remain for capturing a newly ready operand into OC retention
during a wait, but it must not feed another mux ahead of final OC/EX
capture. Once saved, a source must remain authoritative even after
its producer drains or younger producer slots change. Clear saved-ready
state on issue and recovery as before. Capture metadata and all four
operand roles together only on the existing accepted OC issue edge.
Hold current EX operands unchanged during dmem/divider waits; bubbles
and flushes keep the current cleared payload semantics.

Preserve current EX-result-to-OC forwarding for full-rate dependent

title: Predict MEM load values from a tagged word history and wait for WB on misses
motivation:
The champion reaches 203.36 at 85.344 MHz with 4,196,601 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Its worst 17.775 ns path runs from data-memory bank 3
through MEM formatting and forwarding to OC alu_b_val bit 29. LESSONS.md
is absent and predictor history was reviewed. Earlier bimodal/JAL and
narrow MUL prediction won; delayed branch validation and weaker arithmetic
predictions failed acceptance. A load-value predictor can replace the slow
raw-memory bypass with a small local table while retaining every memory
request and exact retirement. A fresh unsigned/narrow-load probe measured
only 79.721 MHz, so this proposal removes the entire raw MEM-to-OC bypass,
including the fallback path, rather than just its upper bits.

through MEM formatting and forwarding to OC alu_b_val bit 29. LESSONS.md
is absent and predictor history was reviewed. Earlier bimodal/JAL and

predictions failed acceptance. A load-value predictor can replace the slow

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one address-tagged load-value predictor at MEM: a 128-entry
direct-mapped history of previously observed raw memory words. Index by
registered effective_addr[8:2], tag with all effective_addr[31:9], and store
32 raw data bits plus a valid bit. Reset valid bits only; do not reset tags
or data, allowing distributed LUT-RAM inference. Mask invalid lookup
qualification so unknown payloads never become a ready forwarding source.
Look up from the existing EX/MEM address register, with no current EX
address adder or forwarding mux before the lookup. Inspect actual Gowin
inference; the table must not become a slow block-RAM read or a large
resettable register mux without measuring that cost.

For a qualified legal aligned load with a matching valid tag, format the
predicted word using the true address lane, width and signedness and feed
that candidate to the existing MEM-to-OC bypass. Qualify readiness with the
actual dmemReady handshake and existing final writer eligibility. On a
miss, keep the matching MEM producer unavailable: OC waits until the exact
load value is registered in MEM/WB and forwards from WB on the next cycle.
Never select live dmemRData as a fallback MEM-to-OC value. Maintain EX's
unavailable-load interlock and nearest-writer priority. Hits preserve the
current one load-use bubble; misses can cost one additional bubble for a
waiting consumer. No prediction bypasses or shortens a memory transaction,
changes an address, skips a request or authorizes a store.

Every load still reads the original bus and commits its exact extracted
value at MEM/WB. Validate a used prediction by comparing its raw predicted
word directly with raw dmemRData on an accepted load, independently of
load formatting. Full-word equality is a sufficient certificate for every
load width and sign; conservatively replay if only unused bytes differ.
Gate mismatch by hit, valid accepted legal aligned load, reg_write and
rd!=x0. Register mismatch into the existing MEM/WB older-repair bit,
ORed with the independently qualified multiply mismatch. Do not put a
shared result-selection mux ahead of equality, or let the comparator
control same-cycle OC forwarding, frontend recovery or memory outputs.
Capture the stored pc_next repair target independently, as today.

Reuse registered older recovery precisely. A failed prediction retires
the original load once with exact data; next-cycle repair redirects to its
PC+4, quarantines younger MEM requests even when unready, squashes younger
EX/OC/decode work and retained sources, suppresses younger branch training
and redirects, and cancels a younger divider or held completion. Correct
hits add no bubble. x0 needs no replay. All original operand, trap, mask,
raw-memory RVFI and consecutive retirement-order fields remain exact.
Miss waiting is an ordinary unavailable-source hold, not a squash or a
whole-pipeline memory stall.

title: Use validity-only recovery for decode and operand payload registers
motivation: The champion achieves 217.29 fitness at 91.186 MHz with 4,196,601 bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its nine-cell data-RAM-to-OC path is now short enough that EX recovery and frontend register control are nearby limits. The full history was reviewed and LESSONS.md is absent. A local exact-load crossbar-fusion prototype kept the canonical CRCs and cycle count but regressed to 68.171 MHz; its worst path traversed EX recovery into ID across 37 cells. The r9s1 crossbar rewrite and r9s2 load predictor similarly exposed EX-to-ID/IF control paths. This proposal therefore targets the existing wide payload reset/enable muxes driven by late recovery, using the same invalid-bubble semantics already enforced by the pipeline's valid bits.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Separate decode and operand-stage payload updates from invalidation. Currently an EX redirect clears every bit of ID/OC and OC/EX and both retained source words, although only validity and saved-ready flags determine whether those words can be used. Remove flush from the wide data reset/select cones. Keep reset clearing, all capture boundaries, exact source routing and every instruction's issue/retirement edge. This is one micro_opt refactoring of pipeline register control, with no additional stage, prediction policy or arithmetic approximation.

In ID, generate the ordinary decode payload hold from id_ex.valid && (hold_oc_ex || !operands_ready), independently of redirect. Wire that hold into ID for its payload update instead of the hazard output that is overridden on recovery. Reset still clears the complete bundle. Otherwise PC, instruction, raw sources, control, immediate, prediction and prepared operands update together only when this ordinary hold is false. The bundle's valid bit separately gives reset/flush highest priority, then accepts in.valid when the ordinary hold is false. Flush may leave arbitrary retained or newly captured metadata with valid=0; no late recovery signal may select zeros on these wide payload registers. Keep redirect-over-hold behavior for validity and fetch PC exactly as today.

In OC, keep current source matches, saved-source precedence, nearest unavailable-producer blocking and the flattened r9s0 candidate networks. When EX is not held, capture metadata and resolved architectural/ALU operands without first muxing an invalid, blocked or flushed payload to all zeros. Qualify only OC/EX valid with in.valid && operands_ready && !flush. When EX is held, retain payload; flush must still clear valid immediately on the next edge. Invalid captured controls/data never authorize execution because all producer, divider, redirect, training, memory and retirement qualifications retain their current valid checks. Remove flush from the retained rs1_value_q/rs2_value_q word clears; keep saved-ready flags cleared on reset, flush and the existing advance edge. Saved data may capture or retain arbitrary unused values during a flush, but no stale word can be selected after its ready flag is cleared. Preserve one-time authoritative retention whenever a live blocked instruction has a resolved operand.

Audit the existing consumers of invalid ID/OC and OC/EX bundles, including operand readiness, EX busy/result handshakes, target traps and source forwarding. Preserve or add scalar valid qualification where an invalid payload could otherwise cause a real effect; do not add a replacement wide output-zero mux. A bubble must produce no architectural write, divider launch, memory request, redirect, branch training or RVFI retirement. Older multiply repair still squashes younger work, beats irrelevant bus stalls and cancels any younger divider transaction. The original valid instruction payload and architectural operands must remain paired through every actual hold and both recovery causes.

Preserve nret=1 and every external port, exact real/ALTOPS arithmetic, decoder default-illegal validation, branch prediction, memory alignment/side-effect checks, bus handshakes, full-rate dependent ALU forwarding, the accepted-load single bubble, sole MEM/WB retirement and consecutive RVFI order. No contract or benchmark changes are allowed.

The falsifiable prediction is identical bracketed CoreMark cycles and an eight-percent median Fmax/fitness gain. Acceptance at unchanged cycles requires median Fmax above 95.380556 MHz and fitness above 227.28534. This estimate needs vendor validation; nearby memory-return and EX arithmetic paths can cap the benefit. Test recovery simultaneous with ordinary holds, unavailable operands, imem/dmem stalls, saved-source retention and held divider completion. Update only incidental assertions that every bit of an invalid OC output is zero: require valid=0 plus disabled architectural effects instead, while retaining all assertions on valid payloads, real holds, reset clearing, exact forwarding, order and progress. Run unchanged formal, trace cosim, canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/bracket gates and all three Gowin placement options.

title: Register exact load returns before formatting and operand forwarding
motivation:
The champion scores 217.29 at median 91.186 MHz with 4,196,601
bracketed CoreMark cycles. Its worst reported 16.487 ns path begins
in data-memory RAM and crosses MEM into OC operand capture. LESSONS.md
is absent. Structural history favors actual register boundaries:
operand preparation, registered multiply recovery and the OC/EX split
won, while delayed redirects and the fetch FIFO failed acceptance.
The latest OC crossbar rewrite and load-value history also regressed.
The remaining direct memory-return path should be cut at an exact-data
register boundary, with its dependency penalty measured explicitly.

hypothesis.hypothesis:

captures the unformatted accepted 32-bit memory word and its two-bit
byte offset into MEM/WB. Move byte/halfword selection and signed/unsigned
extension into WB, operating exclusively on that registered word and
registered width, sign and offset metadata. Use the resulting exact
architectural value for register-file writes, RVFI rd_wdata and the
existing WB-to-OC forwarding source. Keep the single retirement boundary
and pipeline depth; this is one structural load-return retiming.

Remove the live MEM load-result bypass completely. A qualified load
remains an authoritative MEM writer but is unavailable to OC throughout
MEM, including a cycle with dmemReady=1. Never fall back to live bus data
or forward its address as a result. After acceptance, its registered WB
value becomes available through the existing age-ordered forwarding
network. Preserve EX-before-MEM-before-WB priority: a consumer matching
an unavailable nearest load waits instead of reading an older same-rd
writer. Keep MEM forwarding of registered nonload ALU/link/predicted-MUL
results and current EX-result return forwarding unchanged. Dependent
ordinary ALU instructions must still issue at one per ready cycle.

An immediately dependent load consumer pays two dependency bubbles
instead of one when both buses are ready. Independent instructions
still issue normally, and no extra memory transaction or unconditional
load stall is introduced. Retain OC's independent ready/value snapshots
so an unrelated retiring WB source cannot disappear while the other
source waits for the load. Dmem holds keep the waiting request stable;
MEM/WB clears valid without overwriting its retained raw data and lane
metadata, preserving one-time writeback and retirement. Capture raw
data only on the established advancing MEM edge; never accept a load
while the real bus is unready or an older multiply repair quarantines it.

Keep effective addresses, all store data and byte enables, memory
request qualification and alignment traps in their existing stages.
RVFI mem_rdata remains the exact raw accepted word; mem_addr remains
word-aligned with the original lane masks. A new registered load_offset
field must carry the original effective_addr[1:0], because aligned
RVFI mem_addr cannot recover that information. Illegal or misaligned
loads remain nonwriters and make no bus request. x0 never receives a
forwarded value. The formatted result must be exact for LB/LBU/LH/LHU/LW
at every legal byte lane, independently of subsequent bus-data changes.

Preserve nret=1, every external port, original architectural RVFI source
snapshots, strictly consecutive retirement order, decoder defaults and
SYSTEM policy. Keep branch prediction/recovery/training, narrow multiply
prediction, exact MEM product validation and registered quarantine,
divider start/hold/consume/cancel, and all real/ALTOPS arithmetic intact.
Recovery still discards younger OC work and saved operands with existing
priorities; registered load data must never become a wrong-path write.
Do not add a predictor, cache, fetch queue or arithmetic policy change.

The expected eight-percent fitness gain is an unmeasured estimate.
Removing both live-bus formatting and OC fanout from the RAM return
should shorten the limiting path, while the extra load-use bubble costs
some cycles. The main risks are WB formatting plus OC/RF routing and an
EX redirect/return path becoming the new limit. Acceptance requires
(Fmax_new / 91.186) * (4,196,601 / cycles_new) > 1.046. With a three-percent
cycle increase this requires median Fmax above approximately 98.24 MHz;
approximately 101.44 MHz would yield an eight-percent fitness gain.

CRC/validation-literal/MMIO-bracket gates and all three Gowin placements.
Adjust only stage-layout and load-use timing expectations in unit tests;
retain every architectural, arithmetic, trap and memory assertion.

title: Predict ADD/SUB results with a signed 20-bit datapath and registered exact replay
motivation:
The champion reaches 217.29 at 91.186 MHz with 4,196,601 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent and the predictor history was
reviewed. Narrow MUL prediction succeeded; r4's split-carry prediction
failed before registered recovery and the OC/EX boundary existed, and
also altered memory address generation. Fresh isolated load-prediction
probes remove parts of the loaded-data bypass but regress frequency;
their worst paths expose EX arithmetic returning to OC. Predicting a
small integer result can shorten that return path without introducing
another history table or an address correction path.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion reaches 217.29 at 91.186 MHz with 4,196,601 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent and the predictor history was
reviewed. Narrow MUL prediction succeeded; r4's split-carry prediction

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Introduce one stateless computational predictor for ADD/ADDI/AUIPC/SUB
register results. In the EX ALU instance compute ADD and SUB modulo
2^20 from the low twenty bits of the already registered selected ALU
operands, then sign-extend the twenty-bit result to thirty-two bits.
This is advisory arithmetic, not an operand-range assumption. The
candidate is exact whenever the architectural modulo-32-bit result
equals that sign extension; arbitrary wider results remain legal and
are corrected by validation. Use explicit twenty-bit expressions so
synthesis eliminates the ordinary full-width EX ADD/SUB result cone.
Keep the standalone ALU exact by default with an elaboration parameter.

Capture the original selected thirty-two-bit alu_a and alu_b alongside
the predicted result in EX/MEM. These inputs already include PC for
AUIPC, the correct sign-extended immediate for ADDI and architectural
rs2 for register arithmetic. Do not reconstruct immediate decode or
source forwarding in MEM. Forward the predicted result through the
existing EX-to-OC and MEM-to-OC paths with unchanged availability and
successful-prediction latency. Keep original architectural source
snapshots separate for RVFI; no predicted value replaces them.

In MEM calculate exact thirty-two-bit ADD/SUB from those registered
selected operands and always capture the exact result into MEM/WB for
qualifying arithmetic instructions. A shared adder can incorporate
subtraction by complementing b and injecting its carry without two
serial adders: bits [32:1] of {a,1'b1}+{b XOR {32{sub}},sub} implement
a+b for sub=0 and a-b for sub=1. Validate only bits [31:20] against the
captured prediction: the low twenty bits were computed exactly modulo
2^20, so upper-half equality is sufficient for the full result. Do not
place the exact result or equality on an OC forwarding path.

Qualify correction and mismatch strictly as a valid legal reg_write
ADD/SUB operation excluding loads, stores and all jumps. ADDI and AUIPC
are included; JAL/JALR retain their exact PC+4 links even though their
default decoded ALU operation is ADD. For rd=x0 no recovery is needed.
Keep the dedicated full-width effective-address adder, memory requests,
alignment checks, target adders and branch comparisons exactly as today.
Prediction never determines a memory address. LUI, shifts, comparisons,
multiply predictions, exact multiplication and divider protocols are
outside this hypothesis. All M-extension ALTOPS formulas stay exact;
ADD/SUB prediction and validation remain active in formal builds.

Register the qualified upper-bit mismatch at the existing MEM/WB edge,
ORed with the independently qualified multiply mismatch, and retain
unconditional repair-target capture from the original pc_next. The
exact older arithmetic instruction retires once. Existing next-cycle
older recovery replays at its PC+4, quarantines the younger MEM request
even when unready, squashes EX/OC/decode and retained operands, suppresses
younger redirects and branch training, and cancels younger division.
Never let the exact arithmetic comparator control same-cycle frontend,
readiness or memory outputs. Preserve holds and train no new state.

The expected gain is six percent with low confidence, from removing
twelve carry-propagation bits on the EX result-return path. This is an
unmeasured arithmetic hypothesis, not a claim of an evaluated win. It
differs from r4 by replacing the full EX arithmetic result with a narrow
sign-extension candidate, using current registered older recovery and
registered OC operands, and leaving memory addresses exact in EX.
Risks are exact MEM arithmetic becoming critical, added operand-register
routing, a remaining memory bypass limit, and replays on wide sums.
Profile candidate mismatches and measure actual stalled cycles; modest
datapath shortening alone does not establish a fitness improvement.

timing. Acceptance requires (Fmax_new/91.186)*(4,196,601/cycles_new)>1.046.
