OC already has a flattened forwarding/retention/ALU-role network, but an accepted load first traverses MEM lane extraction, sign/zero extension and load/nonload bypass selection before entering that network. LESSONS.md is absent; micro_opt history and recent outcomes were reviewed. The r9 OC flattening won, while r10 delayed load forwarding and validity-only recovery regressed. A fresh isolated MEM-only lane-mask rewrite passed 50,000 randomized complete MEM equivalence cycles but measured only 85.279 MHz median; pre-registering those masks measured 86.664 MHz. Those results reject those standalone changes and motivate removing the remaining MEM-to-OC selection boundary itself.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make one local micro_opt change: fuse exact MEM load formatting and producer selection into OC's existing masked-OR operand capture networks. Retain the current pipeline boundaries, producer ages, bus acceptance and instruction advancement edges. Do not feed a complete formatted MEM load through another wide OC data-selection mux.

Supply OC with the raw io_dmemRData word and the current EX/MEM registered load width, sign flag and effective-address lane, alongside the registered nonload in.alu_result. Keep MEM's original post-trap/post-repair bypass_writer and bypass_ready indications authoritative. These sidebands describe the same MEM instruction as those qualifications. The raw word is usable only on the existing accepted-load capture edge; it is never a predicted, cached, or separately accepted response.

For each OC destination role (architectural rs1, architectural rs2, selected ALU a and selected ALU b), combine that role's existing MEM select with mutually exclusive byte/halfword/word lane controls BEFORE the raw data masks. For ALU a/b, the MEM enable already includes !is_auipc or !alu_src respectively. Form each destination's final balanced OR directly from its saved, EX, WB, ID and PC/immediate candidates, plus MEM raw-word/lane/sign candidates. Include sign extension within those candidates: upper bits select the original byte/halfword sign bit when mem_sext is set, otherwise zero. A word-load candidate uses raw word bits directly. A nonload MEM candidate uses the registered alu_result with the role's MEM select AND !mem_read. Neither a selected byte nor a finished formatted MEM word may feed a following wide role mux. Shared scalar lane decodes are allowed; a shared complete 32-bit formatted result preceding the OC selectors defeats this hypothesis.

Use explicit bit-slice equations, generated masked terms or equivalent balanced reductions so Gowin can map a raw bit or sign bit directly into the final candidate reduction. Fold identical raw-bit contributions together and avoid a serial procedural priority reduction or unnecessary duplicated 32-bit byte selectors. Use the same architectural source networks for one-time retained-source capture, so a load value saved while the other source waits survives changing bus data. The ALU-role networks must read candidate data directly, preserving r9's absence of architectural-value-to-ALU wide muxes.

Preserve EX-over-MEM-over-WB-over-ID producer priority and saved-source precedence. A nearest unavailable producer still blocks capture; readiness qualifies the capture edge, never selects an older writer. Preserve x0, legal/trapping writer qualification, the current single load-use bubble and full-rate dependent ALU forwarding. Keep every OC metadata/control capture, reset, flush, saved-ready clear, hold and advance priority. Independent bus stalls, divider waits and older repair must never pair a raw word with another instruction's lane metadata.

MEM retains its exact formatted read_data for MEM/WB architectural writeback and its existing isolated-module bypass_value behavior. Only the core's OC data wiring changes to bypass the complete MEM formatting result. Keep all memory-side address, replicated store data, byte masks, alignment traps, dmemReady qualification and registered multiply repair/quarantine unchanged. Older repair suppresses younger writers, captures and memory effects as today. Keep exact real/ALTOPS arithmetic, multiplication validation, divider start/hold/consume/cancel, branch prediction/recovery/training, decoder defaults and SYSTEM policy, nret=1 and every top-level port. Preserve original RVFI operands, exact load results/raw words/lane masks and strictly consecutive retirement order. No evaluator or other core changes are permitted.

The expected eight-percent gain has low confidence and is not a measured win. It targets a boundary that the measured MEM-only and predecoded-mask probes did not remove; neither failed probe should be implemented as the final proposal. More candidate terms and control fanout can negate the saved stages, and EX arithmetic/recovery can become the remaining limit. Scheduling should remain identical, but verify actual bracketed cycles rather than assuming them. Acceptance requires (Fmax_new/91.186)*(4,196,601/cycles_new)>1.046; at identical cycles this means median Fmax above 95.380556 MHz and fitness above 227.28534. Run unchanged formal, ready/stalled trace cosim, canonical 2K CoreMark CRC/UART/MMIO-bracket gates and all three Gowin placements. Retain every existing architectural, forwarding, hold, trap and advancement assertion.

title: Register EX control-flow recovery and branch training at EX/MEM
motivation:
The champion scores 217.29 at 91.186 MHz with 4,196,601 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent; the full structural history
and the recent outcomes were reviewed. Several recent variants expose
a 37-38-cell path from registered OC/EX source operands through EX
into fetch or decode control. Registering raw load returns in r10
cost 5.91 percent more cycles and reduced Fmax to 75.784 MHz, so another
load-delivery stage is poorly supported. R2's registered redirects
predated the current predictor and incurred an extra cycle on every
taken transfer. The present frontend already predicts conditional
branches and direct JALs; only mispredictions and JALR need recovery.
Registering that recovery and its predictor-training sideband can
remove the long EX comparator/control path with a smaller cycle cost.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Move the control-flow recovery boundary from combinational EX outputs
to registered EX/MEM sidebands. Continue resolving each branch and
jump exactly from the existing registered OC/EX architectural operands
in EX. Capture the qualified misprediction/JALR recovery bit and its
exact target only when that instruction advances into EX/MEM. Capture
branch-training validity, PC index and actual direction on the same
edge. Fetch redirection, decode/OC flushing and predictor-table writes
must depend exclusively on these registered sidebands and the existing
older registered multiply repair, never on the current EX comparator,
target-adder result or combinational branch-advancement qualification.
This is one structural retiming of control-flow recovery and training.

Preserve the existing prediction policy and predicted_taken metadata.
Correctly predicted conditional branches and aligned direct JALs keep
their current throughput and create no recovery. A conditional direction
mismatch or valid aligned JALR pays exactly one additional recovery
cycle. Keep the resolving instruction's architectural pc_next, jump
link, traps, source operands and destination paired with the registered
repair. Capture the target unconditionally on an advancing edge if that
avoids a comparator-controlled wide-register enable; only the recovery
bit qualifies its use. Illegal and misaligned control transfers must
retain the current trap and sequential-next-PC behavior. Preserve the
current exclusion of misaligned branch targets from predictor training.

In the registered-recovery cycle the resolving branch/jump is in MEM
and must advance into MEM/WB and retire exactly once. Suppress and
invalidate the younger current EX instruction before EX/MEM capture,
and flush both younger OC work and decode, including saved operands.
Install the registered repair target even if imem is unready or the
younger EX instruction would launch or wait for division. Connect this
younger-EX squash to the existing divider cancellation interface, and
suppress younger forwarding eligibility, divider start, combinational
redirect generation and new training capture. Do not squash the older
resolving MEM instruction. Preserve the existing MEM request gating;
no younger load/store may cross EX/MEM on the recovery edge.

A redirect sideband is created only on genuine EX advancement, never
while an older dmem request stalls EX/MEM or a divider is incomplete.
Pending sidebands are consumed once with their owner; clear them on
bubbles, reset and recovery so a held or drained slot cannot redirect
or train twice. Keep older multiply repair highest priority: it chooses
the existing multiply replay PC, quarantines younger MEM effects,
discards younger branch recovery and training, and cancels younger
division. A pending branch's own registered recovery must not mask its
legitimate registered training pulse merely because it squashes younger
EX work. Train the surviving registered branch exactly once, including
on its own recovery cycle. Update the existing 64-entry counters from
registered index/direction with unchanged saturating transitions and
read-before-write semantics; the one-cycle later update is the sole
prediction-timing consequence, with no new predictor state or policy.

Preserve EX-result-to-OC and accepted MEM-load forwarding, full-rate
dependent ordinary ALU issue, the existing one-bubble load-use policy,
exact MEM multiplication and registered validation/quarantine, all real
and ALTOPS arithmetic, stable waiting dmem transactions and WB retention.
Keep nret=1, every external port, the sole retirement boundary, consecutive
RVFI order, exact source snapshots, default-illegal decoder and SYSTEM
policy, alignment checks and every hard invariant. No evaluation or
benchmark contract file changes are proposed.

The expected seven-percent fitness gain is an unmeasured estimate with
low confidence. Removing high-fanout EX recovery/training cones should
improve timing, but the MEM load bypass or EX-result return can remain
limiting. Later misprediction/JALR recovery and delayed counter updates
cost cycles. Acceptance requires (Fmax_new / 91.186) multiplied by
(4,196,601 / cycles_new) to exceed 1.046. With a two-percent cycle increase
the median vendor Fmax must exceed approximately 97.29 MHz; approximately
99.52 MHz would give seven percent higher fitness. Measure both the
bracketed cycle count and all three Gowin placements. Run unchanged
formal, unit suites, ready/stalled trace cosim and canonical 2K CoreMark
CRC, completion-literal, MMIO-bracket and bounded-access validation.

title: Distribute bimodal predictor training into prediction and confidence bit planes
motivation:
The champion's 64-entry bimodal predictor has a shared indexed counter
read/modify/write training port in addition to its fetch lookup. Its
saturation comparisons, increment/decrement and broadcast write data
can be replaced by local state transitions without changing accuracy.
LESSONS.md is absent and predictor-category history was reviewed. The
r2 instruction-qualified direction predictor succeeded; r8 later branch
validation and recent value-prediction attempts regressed. Local probes
also rejected a larger gshare table and projected branch comparisons:
both added routing or validation cost and lost median frequency. Focus
this hypothesis solely on the predictor's physical state/update topology.

The champion's 64-entry bimodal predictor has a shared indexed counter

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Retain exactly the current 64-entry bimodal prediction policy, PC[7:2]
index, instruction qualification, weakly-taken reset and EX training
event. Replace each binary saturating counter with two locally updated
bits: prediction P and strong-confidence S. Encode ordinary counter
states 00,01,10,11 respectively as (P,S)=(0,1),(0,0),(1,0),(1,1).
Fetch reads only a packed 64-bit prediction plane; the confidence plane
is read only by its corresponding entry's local transition logic.

For a qualified training event with outcome T, update the selected entry
from its pre-edge state using P_next = S ? P : T and
S_next = !(P XOR T). These equations exactly implement the existing
two-bit saturating predictor, including hysteresis and saturation.
Reset every P to one and every S to zero. Implement a generate block
with a constant six-bit index per entry and one local write qualification
branch_train_en && branch_train_index == ENTRY_INDEX. Every unselected
entry holds. Avoid a dynamically indexed counter read for training,
numeric increment/decrement, saturation tests and a globally broadcast
counter-result bus. Do not add a pipeline stage or delay training.

Keep accepting-edge prediction based on pre-write state, including a
same-index lookup and training event. Preserve EX's exact branch
comparator, actual-taken training qualification, advancement/hold
gating, direction-XOR repair, direct target alignment checks and older
multiply-repair priority. Do not change predictor capacity, indexing,
branch/JAL/JALR policy, fetch acceptance, metadata, pipeline boundaries,
arithmetic, memory behavior or recovery. This is one predictor state
architecture change, with identical logical predictions for every legal
sequence of lookup and training events.

The expected six-percent gain is an estimate from eliminating the second
table read mux and shared counter update datapath, reducing predictor
LUTs and routing without adding CoreMark cycles. Explicit local update
topology matters: merely rewriting an indexed binary-counter increment
into Boolean arithmetic is insufficient. Check the vendor netlist for
separate local confidence transitions and a prediction-only fetch mux.
This may still be limited by the existing MEM-to-OC or EX recovery path,
and physical placement can outweigh the small predictor area reduction;
no win is claimed before implementation-phase evaluation.

Preserve nret=1, all external ports, exact RVFI operands/results/order,
decoder defaults and trap discipline, memory side effects, divider
transaction/cancellation and real/ALTOPS arithmetic, and every hard
invariant. Exhaustively compare all four states and both outcomes with
the original saturating-counter transition model, then test disabled
training, reset, saturation, alternating outcomes, aliases, same-edge
lookup/update and acceptance holds. Retain every existing predictor and
pipeline assertion. Run unchanged formal, ready/stalled trace cosim,
canonical 2K CoreMark CRC/bracket/completion validation and all three
Gowin placements. Expected bracketed cycles are exactly 4196601.
At unchanged cycles, acceptance requires median Fmax above 95.380556 MHz;
in general require (Fmax_new/91.186)*(4196601/cycles_new) > 1.046.

title: Shorten exact EX arithmetic with block carry lookahead
motivation:
The champion delivers 217.29 iterations/second at median 91.186 MHz
and 4,196,601 bracketed CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent. The
micro_opt history and the recent arithmetic, recovery and load-return
attempts were reviewed. R9's flattened OC selection improved fitness,
but several later variants expose 37-38-cell paths from OC/EX operands
through EX arithmetic into OC or frontend control. Registering branch
recovery in r11 reduced Fmax and increased cycles; approximate ADD/SUB
in r10 also regressed. The existing full-width inferred carry chains
are an unaddressed opportunity to shorten those paths without replay,
an additional stage or a different scheduling policy.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion delivers 217.29 iterations/second at median 91.186 MHz
and 4,196,601 bracketed CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent. The

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace full-width inferred EX addition/subtraction and magnitude
comparison chains with one exact combinational block carry-lookahead
topology. Partition 32-bit operands into eight four-bit blocks. In
parallel obtain each block's carry generate from its carry-zero local
addition and its propagate as the AND of the operand-bit XORs. Combine
these generate/propagate pairs with a balanced prefix network at
distances 1, 2 and 4. Derive every block's incoming carry directly from
its prefix and the operation's initial carry; never ripple carry
through eight blocks. Compute each block's sums for incoming carry
zero and one independently and select with its exact prefix carry.
Use explicitly sized expressions that avoid two serial additions for
a+b+carry. A five-bit carry-zero sum and bits [5:1] of the six-bit
addition {1'b0,a_block,1'b1}+{1'b0,b_block,1'b1} give the required
carry-zero and carry-one alternatives. All results are exact modulo
2^32 for arbitrary operands, including overflow and long carry runs.

Provide elaboration-time fixed add/subtract variants of the helper.
Subtraction complements the second operand and starts with carry one;
unsigned a<b is the inverse of its final carry. Signed a<b selects
a[31] when operand signs differ, and otherwise the unsigned result.
Preserve separately parallel add and subtract paths where the current
RTL has them; do not insert a late opcode-controlled operand inversion
in front of every arithmetic operation merely to share hardware.
Equality and inequality stay balanced bit reductions. Branch BGE/BGEU
invert the corresponding exact less-than result. Do not derive signed
comparisons from a subtraction sign without overflow correction.

Apply the helper to the ALU's base ADD/SUB/SLT/SLTU and to EX's current
source-address, JALR, PC-relative target and PC+4 arithmetic. Share
genuinely identical EX sums such as pc+imm, but keep the dedicated
effective-address path independent of the general ALU result mux.
Current registered OC/EX operands remain the inputs; current EX/MEM
and OC capture edges remain the outputs. Preserve full-rate dependent
ALU forwarding, the single load-use bubble, exact target/alignment
decisions and the same combinational redirect/training event. The
experiment is solely an exact arithmetic topology micro-optimization.

Keep the registered divider's datapath, latency, transaction protocol
and cancellation unchanged. Keep multiplication prediction, exact MEM
validation and registered repair/quarantine unchanged. Preserve all
RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS identities, default-illegal decode, SYSTEM policy,
saved-source and nearest-producer rules, bus stalls, all memory effects,
nret=1, external ports, exact RVFI data and consecutive retirement order.
No benchmark, wrapper, evaluator, timing constraint or other core edits
are permitted. Do not weaken existing tests or invariants.

The estimated eight-percent fitness improvement has low confidence.
This topology attacks both EX-result return and branch decision carry
chains without increasing cycles, but prefix fanout, duplicated local
sums and placement pressure can outweigh shorter logic, and the MEM
load bypass may remain limiting. Inspect the Gowin netlist/timing to
verify short local carry chains and balanced inter-block carry logic;
source-level reassociation alone is insufficient. Run the unchanged
formal, unit, ready/stalled cosim and canonical 2K CoreMark CRC/UART/
MMIO-bracket gates, then all three vendor placements. Expected counted
cycles remain 4,196,601. Acceptance requires fitness above 227.28534,
or median Fmax above 95.380556 MHz at identical cycles; in general
require (Fmax_new/91.186)*(4196601/cycles_new)>1.046. No measured win
is claimed before implementation and vendor evaluation.

title: Register producer dependency routes before operand collection
motivation:
The champion scores 217.29 at 91.186 MHz with 4,196,601 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent; the full structural history was
reviewed. R5's registered bypass decisions improved fitness by 12.12
percent, but R8's successful OC/EX split replaced those decisions with
live EX/MEM/WB destination comparisons in OC. R9 already flattened the
data crossbar, so another mux rewrite repeats an explored approach.
R11's registered branch recovery instead exposed a 17.497 ns path from
a MEM destination register through u_oc/u_forward into an OC operand
register. Recent variants also expose EX-result-to-OC return paths.
Moving dependency identity ahead of operand collection can remove
destination comparison and priority construction from capture without
the extra load-use or recovery cycles that hurt R10 and R11.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Retime producer identity resolution into the existing ID-to-OC capture
boundary. Replace OC's live source-address versus producer-destination
comparisons with a small registered dependency-route matrix: for each
architectural source, record matching potential older writers in the
EX, MEM and WB slots that will exist immediately after the capture
edge. Let id_stage own these six bits in its ID/OC payload register,
plus two registered source-is-zero bits. Register all three matches
rather than only the winning match,
because a nominal younger writer can subsequently be disqualified by
a target or access alignment trap. Use registered x0 qualification.
Keep the current flattened OC data crossbar and all pipeline boundaries.
This is one structural retiming of dependency selection and its state,
with no additional instruction, dependency or recovery latency.

Construct the matrix from actual next-cycle pipeline occupancy, using
the same acceptance, hold, bubble and squash decisions as the payload
registers. On a normal simultaneous advance, the current decoded OC
instruction becomes next EX, current EX becomes next MEM, and current
MEM becomes next WB. Compare the newly fetched source addresses against
those respective destinations before its ID/OC capture. A held EX or
MEM remains its own next-cycle occupant; an incomplete divider emits a
MEM bubble while retaining EX; an accepted divider completion transfers
its original destination and payload to MEM. A dmem hold retains MEM
and EX and clears next WB validity. An empty OC may still accept one
instruction while EX is blocked, so do not assume that decode capture
implies every older stage advanced. Old WB is covered by the existing
write-first register-file snapshot at this edge, not a stale next-WB
dependency. Derive nominal writer membership only from valid, legal,
nonzero-rd decoded instructions that can write; do not put current EX
target/effective-address arithmetic into the ID match-register enables.

In OC, mask each registered candidate with its current stage's final
writer eligibility after the existing illegal/target/access checks.
Select the nearest eligible candidate in EX, MEM, WB order, then the
original write-first ID snapshot. Retain lower-priority matches until
a source is resolved, so a trapping nearer instruction cannot hide a
surviving older writer. Readiness remains separate from identity: a
matching eligible but unavailable load or divider blocks that source
and must never fall through to an older same-rd value. A saved-ready
source suppresses every live route; x0 selects zero. Remove producer
destination-address inputs from OC/forward_unit: source-versus-producer
equality comparisons exist only ahead of the route registers. Existing
scalar final-writer and result-ready flags still qualify the routes.

When OC holds, migrate its unresolved match bits using actual producer
transitions on each edge: retain a held producer's bit, move an
advancing EX bit to MEM and an advancing MEM bit to WB, and remove
drained or invalidated occupancy. Compute transitions from pre-edge
state, including simultaneous movements and bubbles. This small-state
migration runs while the decoded payload is held; it is not frozen by
stall_id. The architectural source addresses and original data snapshots
remain held. No younger
instruction can overtake held OC, so no new unresolved dependency may
appear behind these original candidates. Preserve the existing
independent per-source ready/value snapshots: capture a ready source
before WB drains even when EX is held or the other source is blocked,
and never reselect it. Loading a new decoded instruction replaces both
matrices atomically with its source snapshots and metadata. Reset and
either recovery clear matrices and saved state with the existing
payload priorities. Never update a held instruction's identity from
newly changing imem data or a guessed unconditional stage shift.

Preserve full-rate dependent ordinary ALU issue through the current
EX-result return and the one-bubble immediate load-use policy through
accepted, formatted MEM-load forwarding. Keep all four OC operand roles
selected before OC/EX, using the current parallel masked OR networks;
no forwarding mux moves into current EX arithmetic. Branches, JALR,
stores and MUL/DIV use the exact architectural source values. Preserve
current branch prediction, combinational EX recovery/training, narrow
multiplication prediction, exact MEM validation and registered repair,
divider start/hold/consume/cancel, WB retention and real/ALTOPS arithmetic.
Older multiply repair remains highest priority and quarantines younger
MEM side effects; branch recovery flushes younger OC and decode without
suppressing the resolving instruction. Keep nret=1, all external ports,
decoder defaults and SYSTEM policy, alignment checks, RVFI operand and
memory records, consecutive retirement order and every hard invariant.

The estimated ten-percent fitness improvement is unmeasured. It comes
from registering dependency comparison ahead of OC, rather than adding
a load-delivery stage or delaying recovery. Final writer qualification,
route-mask fanout, EX arithmetic or memory-return routing may remain
limiting, and a naive next-state implementation can create a new ID
control path. Acceptance requires (Fmax_new / 91.186) multiplied by
(4,196,601 / cycles_new) to exceed 1.046. With unchanged CoreMark cycles,
the acceptance threshold is about 95.381 MHz and ten-percent improvement
requires about 100.305 MHz. Confirm unchanged scheduling and exact
semantics with unit suites, unchanged formal, ready/stalled trace cosim,
canonical 2K CoreMark CRCs, UART validation literal, MMIO brackets and
bounded accesses, then measure all three vendor Gowin placements.

title: Reduce branch-table aliases with a compact folded-PC bimodal predictor
motivation:
The champion scores 217.29 at 91.186 MHz with 4,196,601 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent; the predictor history and recent
outcomes were reviewed. Delayed control-flow validation, arithmetic
replay and confidence-plane counter recoding have regressed. The
existing 64-entry direction table indexes only PC[7:2], so unrelated
branches separated by 256 bytes repeatedly overwrite the same counters.
A smaller table with a folded PC index can reduce that interference
while reducing lookup and training mux size. This targets the predictor
policy and capacity without adding a pipeline stage or recovery latency.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the 64-entry PC[7:2] conditional direction table with 32 ordinary
two-bit saturating counters indexed by PC[6:2] XOR PC[11:7]. Reset all
counters to weakly taken, retain the current increment/decrement and
saturation rules, and train only on the existing qualified advancing
EX conditional-branch event. Compute the same folded index from the
resolving branch's original PC; do not train using the live fetch PC.
Keep the binary counter representation and existing dynamic update
implementation rather than repeating the failed confidence-plane design.

Fetch still qualifies prediction against the exact raw branch encoding,
requires an aligned immediate target, and uses the selected counter's
high bit. Direct JAL prediction remains exact from its immediate, JALR
keeps current EX resolution, and all other instructions predict PC+4.
Carry the existing accepted predicted_taken bit with its instruction;
EX keeps exact comparison and direction-XOR recovery. No history state,
target bank, speculative operand or extra validation stage is introduced.

Prediction and instruction capture remain coupled to fetch_accept.
Preserve pre-edge lookup on simultaneous training, including same-index
events; held instructions train once only on actual advancement.
Preserve imem/dmem stalls, operand retention, divider cancellation,
registered older multiply recovery, wrong-path effect suppression and
all existing recovery priorities. Aliases affect accuracy only because
targets are always calculated from the actual instruction's immediate.

The expected six-percent fitness gain has low confidence. A reduced
lookup/update network may improve placement and clock frequency, and
spreading high-PC aliases can reduce recovery cycles despite the smaller
table. XOR delay, reduced capacity and the existing EX/MEM-to-OC limits
are the main risks. Profile direction errors and compare actual stalled
bracketed cycles before assuming the new index is beneficial. Require
(Fmax_new/91.186)*(4196601/cycles_new) > 1.046 for acceptance.

Preserve nret=1, every external port, decoder defaults and reserved
encoding traps, exact arithmetic and ALTOPS behavior, actual RVFI
operands/results/next-PC/order, memory transactions and every invariant.
Retain all existing architectural assertions and run unchanged formal,
unit tests, ready/stalled trace cosim, canonical 2K CoreMark CRC/MMIO
bracket/completion/bounded-access validation and median Gowin timing.

title: Remove false OC dependencies on unused instruction source fields
motivation:
The champion reaches 217.29 fitness at 91.186 MHz and 4,196,601 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent. The micro_opt history includes
successful flattened OC selection, but validity-only recovery, fused
load formatting and block carry lookahead subsequently regressed.
OC still resolves both raw instruction source fields for every opcode.
Immediate and upper-immediate bits can therefore falsely match an
unavailable older load, stall issue and keep unnecessary bypass routes
active even when that register is not an execution operand. Removing
those false dependencies is a local refinement of the existing resolver.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Register two semantic execution-source-use bits with each ID/OC payload.
Derive them only from positively validated decoded instructions: OP uses
both sources; OP-IMM, LOAD and JALR use rs1 only; STORE and BRANCH use
both; LUI, AUIPC, direct JAL, FENCE and accepted EBREAK use neither.
Illegal encodings use neither and retain their existing trap behavior.
Store data remains a genuine rs2 operand despite alu_src selecting an
immediate. Do not infer source use solely from alu_src or reg_write.

In OC, feed an effective zero source address to forward_unit for each
unused execution source, while retaining the original unmasked addresses
in the instruction metadata. This disables its producer comparisons and
data candidates, makes its readiness unconditional and prevents it from
retaining an unnecessary value. Used sources keep the existing nearest
qualified EX/MEM/WB producer, unavailable-nearest blocking, x0 behavior,
independently saved values and flattened architectural/ALU-role muxes.
Preserve all pipeline boundaries and advancement priorities. Ordinary
dependent ALU issue and true single-bubble load use remain unchanged;
only a previously false source dependency may remove an issue bubble.

The unchanged ISS compares raw source addresses and pre-instruction data
even for unused fields. Preserve that exact RVFI contract: add two
verification-only asynchronous retirement read ports to reg_file, with
no write-first bypass. Address them with the retiring instruction's raw
source addresses. Its storage already contains all older WB writes and
has not yet accepted this instruction's own write, so these ports expose
the precise pre-retirement architectural values. For used sources retain
the existing captured execution values; for unused sources select these
retirement reads in core's RVFI outputs. Preserve raw addresses, x0 and
reset semantics. Qualify the choice with the retiring instruction's
semantic source-use metadata. The added reads must feed RVFI only and
be pruned from the timed memory-output netlist; no new functional read
port, shadow scoreboard or commit delay is required. Never zero unused
RVFI source data or alter the reference, wrapper or comparison checks.

Preserve decoder default-illegal policy, every reserved-encoding and
SYSTEM check, exact real and ALTOPS arithmetic, branch prediction and
recovery, multiplier validation/repair/quarantine, divider transactions,
bus handshakes, memory alignment checks, sole nret=1 retirement boundary
and consecutive RVFI order. Flush and older repair still discard all
younger payload and saved-source state, and downstream holds still apply.

The estimated six-percent fitness gain has low confidence. Fewer false
load dependencies can improve iterations/cycle, while inactive unused
routes reduce forwarding-control activity and fanout. Source-use gating
can itself increase timing depth, and the true-dependency rate may leave
little cycle headroom. Measure both factors instead of assuming a win:
acceptance requires (Fmax_new/91.186)*(4196601/cycles_new) > 1.046.
Run unchanged formal, unit and field-by-field ready/stalled cosim, the
canonical 2K CoreMark CRC/UART/MMIO-bracket/bounded-access checks and all
three Gowin placements. Preserve existing assertions on real sources
and exact raw RVFI fields; adapt only artificial stage fixtures that
deliberately treat immediate or PC fields as execution dependencies.

title: Execute exact multiplication in two cycles using the existing OC operand registers
motivation:
The champion reaches 217.29 iter/s at 91.186 MHz and 4,196,601 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Recent worst paths repeatedly traverse EX arithmetic
returning to OC or MEM-to-OC capture. Attempts to register OC dependency
routes, delay load forwarding, and register branch recovery regressed.
The earlier r3 structural multiplier used separate launch operand
registers and added two issue cycles per MUL, reaching 58.572 MHz and
4,389,122 cycles on a much older pipeline. The current pipeline already
supplies registered, fully resolved OC/EX operands. This permits a
cheaper multiplication transaction while removing the speculative EX
multiplier, the three exact MEM products, mismatch comparison, recovery
muxing, and younger-memory quarantine from the timed circuit.
The champion's reported narrow_product endpoint is an absorbed operand
register; it does not prove that DSP multiplication itself is the worst
path. The proposed benefit depends on changing the return datapath and
reducing validation/recovery placement pressure, and must be measured.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace speculative multiplication and subsequent MEM validation with
one exact registered multiplier executed from the existing OC/EX operand
registers. This is one structural change to multiplication execution
and completion. Keep ordinary ALU operations, load delivery, branch
prediction and recovery, and the divider at their existing boundaries.
Do not add an operand-launch register: OC/EX already owns the exact
architectural operands and remains occupied until completion.

In the first EX cycle of a legal MUL-family instruction, compute one
unsigned 32-by-32 product from in.rs1_val and in.rs2_val and capture its
complete 64-bit value on the edge. A small registered completion state
now makes its low or high half available. In the next EX cycle, forward
the registered result to OC and transfer the original instruction into
EX/MEM on the same edge that releases OC/EX. MUL and MULHU therefore cost
exactly one additional issue cycle relative to the champion when the
memory bus is ready. There must be no redundant operand-capture edge or
additional result-copy edge. Remove every combinational multiplication
from the current EX-result return to OC and from MEM. The multiply cone
must terminate at its product register, with no completion-control or
frontend fanout from its data or comparison results.

For MULHSU and MULH, derive the exact signed high word from the registered
unsigned product using high_signed = high_unsigned - (a[31] ? b : 0)
for MULHSU, and a further subtraction of (b[31] ? a : 0) for MULH.
Put each correction subtraction on its own registered step, rather
than chaining corrections after the multiplier or in the OC bypass.
The held OC/EX sources supply original full-width a and b throughout.
MUL and MULHU skip correction states. Preserve all RV32M exceptional
cases and exact modulo-32-bit results. Under RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS use the
existing exact four formulas from the original registered operands and
the same bounded, held completion interface; keep the standalone ALU's
arithmetic coverage and ALTOPS branch consistent.

Launch once when a valid legal multiply occupies EX, no older memory
hold prevents initial advancement, and the unit is idle. Hold OC/EX
while the product or correction is incomplete, but allow older MEM/WB
work to drain. When MEM can advance, emit a fully cleared EX/MEM bubble
during incomplete execution instead of replaying an older request.
Once launched, computation continues independently of dmem readiness;
retain product, operation, completion and original payload until the
established EX/MEM acceptance edge. Completion and its destination are
authoritative producers: bypass_w_en remains qualified while waiting,
bypass_ready is false until the registered exact result is available,
and a matching younger consumer cannot fall through to an older writer.
When complete and MEM accepts, use that result for both EX/MEM and the
existing EX-to-OC return. Clear the occupied transaction on consumption
while advancing OC/EX on that same edge, preventing a held MUL restart.
Preserve independent OC source snapshots while another source waits.

Delete multiply prediction/validation from the instantiated datapath and
remove registered mul_repair, its target selection, and its quarantine
gates. No instruction receives an approximate product, so there is no
multiply replay. MEM now passes the registered exact ALU result for all
MUL-family operations. Keep ordinary EX branch recovery unchanged and
retain reset/cancel behavior for outstanding arithmetic; a flushed or
invalid instruction must never launch or consume a transaction. Keep
multiplication and division mutually exclusive in the single occupied
EX slot, with distinct completion ownership. Preserve real dmem holds,
stable requests, WB retention, existing accepted-load forwarding and
one-bubble load-use behavior. Ordinary dependent ALU chains retain
one-per-ready-cycle issue.

Preserve nret=1 and every top-level port, default-illegal decoding,
SYSTEM legality, alignment traps, original RVFI source snapshots,
memory records, PC successors and strictly consecutive retirement
order. Change only allowed RTL and test/test_*.py files; all correctness,
benchmark, stall-generator, wrapper and timing contracts remain intact.

Prior profiling counted 93,960 MULs and no DIV/REM in the measured run.
One extra issue cycle per low-word MUL is about 2.24 percent of the
champion's cycle count before overlap with existing stalls. With that
conservative estimate, acceptance requires median Fmax above about
97.52 MHz, and a ten-percent fitness gain requires about 102.55 MHz.
Removing both speculative return arithmetic and exact MEM validation
should reduce DSP placement pressure and repair-control fanout, but
live MEM loads and ordinary EX arithmetic can remain limiting. The gain

title: Predict relational branch conditions with 8-bit comparison and registered exact repair
motivation:
The champion scores 217.29 at 91.186 MHz with 4,196,601 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent and predictor history was reviewed.
Smaller folded-PC tables, counter recoding and delayed control-flow
validation regressed. A return profile finds only 13,735 timed JALRs,
so return prediction alone has insufficient upside. Ordinary direction
policy improvements also save too few errors to justify larger tables.
The current full-width relational branch comparisons feed same-cycle
EX redirect, frontend flush and predictor training. A computational
branch-condition predictor can shorten that feedback while retaining
immediate EX correction of ordinary fetch-direction mistakes.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion scores 217.29 at 91.186 MHz with 4,196,601 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent and predictor history was reviewed.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Introduce one stateless computational predictor for relational branch
conditions. Keep BEQ and BNE exact with their existing full-width
equality checks. For BLTU/BGEU compare only rs1[7:0] and rs2[7:0],
complementing the less-than result for BGEU. For BLT/BGE use the true
32-bit sign bits: when rs1[31] differs from rs2[31], signed less-than
is rs1[31]; otherwise predict from unsigned low-8-bit less-than.
Complement this result for BGE. Read only registered OC/EX operands,
with no new forwarding or operand-range assumptions. Wider values
remain legal and are always checked against exact execution.

EX uses the provisional branch condition to correct the accepted fetch
direction immediately, using the existing direction-XOR recovery and
exact PC+immediate target. Qualify provisional taken with valid, legal
branch encoding and target alignment. Keep JAL/JALR resolution, link
values and alignment traps exact in EX. Preserve current EX advancement,
dmem/divider hold gating, older registered recovery priority and flush
behavior. Unlike r8s2, ordinary bimodal direction errors still recover
in EX; only a wrong computed relational condition needs late repair.

Capture the raw provisional condition, before alignment qualification,
in the existing EX/MEM branch_taken field, together with original
full-width architectural rs1/rs2 and the
existing exact branch_target. Existing bundles already carry these
fields, so no extra operand bank or full-width prediction target is
needed. EX must not declare a conditional branch illegal based on its
approximate condition: determine conditional target traps exactly in
MEM. A known misaligned target cannot be provisionally taken in EX.

In MEM form the exact full-width condition by lexicographic validation.
Compare original operand upper bits [31:8]. If they are equal, the
captured raw low-byte condition is already exact. Otherwise compare
those upper 24 bits signed for BLT/BGE or unsigned for BLTU/BGEU,
complementing less-than for greater-or-equal. The upper comparison
decides the full result whenever upper bits differ. BEQ/BNE reuse
their captured full-width exact condition. This is exact for arbitrary
32-bit operands; no range certificate or prediction assumption is
accepted. It avoids a redundant second low-byte comparator in MEM.
Actual effective taken requires a legal branch, true exact condition
and aligned target.
Set the final trap for an exactly taken misaligned conditional target;
its architectural successor is PC+4. For every conditional branch,
commit exact pc_next as actual target or PC+4, and preserve original
RVFI operands, instruction and retirement order. Compare actual
effective-taken against captured raw provisional condition AND target
alignment, reconstructing the precise effective direction used in EX.
A direction mismatch becomes a registered MEM/WB repair, ORed with
the existing independently qualified multiply mismatch. Capture the
exact branch successor in the same repair-target register. A condition
mismatch that leaves the effective successor unchanged needs no replay.

The validating older branch retires once with exact next-PC and trap
fields. On the next cycle reuse existing older recovery to redirect to
that exact successor, quarantine younger MEM requests even if unready,
squash younger EX/OC/decode and saved operands, suppress younger EX
redirects and cancel a younger divider or held completion. Correct
provisional conditions add no recovery cycle. Branches write no integer
destination, so exact MEM branch validation must have no combinational
path into OC writer eligibility, bypass data/readiness or memory bus
enables. Express MEM writer qualification from original control and
memory-alignment checks, explicitly excluding branches; apply exact
conditional trap state only to the registered retirement payload.

Move conditional predictor training to a registered MEM/WB event with
original PC[7:2] and exact actual direction. Generate it once when a
legal aligned branch is accepted by MEM, excluding hold_wb, invalid
bubbles and older recovery. Consume each registered event once in IF
even if the following instruction stalls. A branch's own ordinary EX
repair must not discard its eventual training. A pending event from a
valid older branch may train during younger recovery; quarantined
younger branches generate none. Read the then-current two-bit counter
when consuming the event, preserving consecutive same-index updates
and pre-edge fetch lookup semantics. Retain all 64 entries, PC[7:2]
indexing, binary saturation, weakly-taken reset and immediate JAL policy.

An architectural profile of the unchanged canonical 2K, -O3,
ten-iteration ELF finds 529,588 timed conditional branches. The proposed
full-sign-aware low-byte comparator disagrees on 4,723 outcomes when
BEQ/BNE remain exact, about 0.89 percent of branches. This is a sequential reference
profile, not a measured RTL cycle saving, Fmax result or correctness
proof. Fewer than 0.13 percent of branches require arithmetic validation
correction in that profile. Delayed table training and wrong-path
executions can change RTL behavior. The expected six-percent fitness
gain has low confidence and depends on removing full-width comparison
from immediate recovery/training rather than improved direction accuracy.
Exact MEM comparison, control fanout and the existing load-to-OC path
remain timing risks. Require
(Fmax_new/91.186)*(4196601/cycles_new) > 1.046 for acceptance.

An initial isolated 16-bit prototype completed stalled CoreMark with 4,198,165
bracketed cycles, all five canonical CRCs, the validation literal and
no out-of-bounds accesses. This is 1,564 extra cycles, about 0.037 percent.
It also passed full RVFI trace comparison for selftest and all three
random programs with both ready buses and independent stalls. These
preliminary checks do not replace unchanged formal, directed prediction
recovery tests or median Gowin fitness evaluation. Its single placement-0
timing was 84.234 MHz, below the champion; its worst path remained
MEM-to-OC with an EX recovery path close behind. The final proposed
eight-bit EX predictor and upper-only MEM validator specifically reduce
that recovery logic and duplicated validation, but a win is unproven.
Record final prototype results below if available; do not reuse the
initial 16-bit cycle count as the final candidate's measured result.

Preserve nret=1, all external ports, decoder default-illegal and reserved
encodings, SYSTEM rules, exact real/ALTOPS arithmetic, bus handshakes,
memory alignment and every hard invariant. Keep comparator prediction
active in formal builds and validate every branch with full-width
semantics there too using the exact split comparison; add no symbolic
range or outcome assumptions.
Run unchanged formal, meaningful directed unit tests, ready/stalled
trace cosim, canonical CoreMark CRC/MMIO/bracket/completion/bounded-access
checks and median vendor Gowin timing. Retain every existing architectural
assertion, adapting only internal layouts or prediction-specific timing
expectations to the explicit provisional/validation stages.

motivation:
The champion achieves 217.29 fitness at 91.186 MHz and 4,196,601

flattening shortened MEM-to-OC capture, but recent worst paths also
start at registered EX operation bits and traverse the ALU into OC.

then selects multiplication or a jump link before OC selects the

dependency gating regressed. Predecoding result selection across

hypothesis.hypothesis:

OC/EX boundary, and replace the nested ALU-result, multiplication and
jump-link selections with one parallel masked-OR result network.
This is a local exact result-selection micro-optimization: retain

and jump link. Generate them from the validated decoded controls.

already registered EX ALU operands. Preserve the existing inferred
add/subtract/comparison and shift expressions, avoiding a new carry
topology or a shared opcode-controlled operand inversion. Include

single exact-selected value to both EX bypass_value and EX/MEM
alu_result; remove the outer jump/multiply ternary chains. Leave

redirect and training unchanged. A helper module may hold this

title: Use MEM/WB as a second operand bank without adding a load-use bubble
motivation:
The champion scores 217.29 iter/s at 91.186 MHz and 4,196,601 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path starts at data RAM and runs
through MEM formatting and OC operand capture; recent experiments also
expose EX-result return paths. The r10 structural attempt removed live
MEM load forwarding by waiting for WB, but added 247,872 cycles and
reduced Fmax to 75.784 MHz. Fusing load formatting into OC masks in r11
preserved cycles but reached only 82.934 MHz. The useful structural
opportunity is to separate the accepted load's data register from the
ordinary OC operand registers without delaying its dependent consumer.
Reusing the existing formatted MEM/WB load register avoids another
response register and an additional load-qualified clock enable.
This proposal has not been implemented or timed. LESSONS.md is absent;
the structural and related load-delivery history was reviewed instead.

hypothesis.motivation:
The champion scores 217.29 iter/s at 91.186 MHz and 4,196,601 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. Its reported worst path starts at data RAM and runs
through MEM formatting and OC operand capture; recent experiments also
expose EX-result return paths. The r10 structural attempt removed live
MEM load forwarding by waiting for WB, but added 247,872 cycles and
reduced Fmax to 75.784 MHz. Fusing load formatting into OC masks in r11
preserved cycles but reached only 82.934 MHz. The useful structural
opportunity is to separate the accepted load's data register from the
ordinary OC operand registers without delaying its dependent consumer.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace live MEM-load-to-OC data forwarding with references to the
existing MEM/WB load register and per-source bank bits at OC/EX. Keep
the existing fetch/decode -> OC -> EX -> MEM -> WB topology, one-issue
rate, sole retirement boundary and normal load acceptance edge. This
is one structural change to operand storage and load rendezvous.

Reuse the existing MEM/WB read_data register as the shared load bank.
On an accepted, aligned, legal MEM load, its normal capture already
registers the exact formatted architectural value using the current
width, sign flag and byte offset. Export that registered read_data
directly, before the WB ALU/load result mux. Keep every MEM/WB capture,
hold, bubble and repair rule intact; do not add a response queue or
register. A new reference is legal only when the real load request is
accepted and not quarantined by older multiply repair. The reference
has a one-cycle lifetime, so later MEM/WB overwrites remain safe after
consumption or materialization. Raw memory records stay unchanged.
The live data bus and formatted load must have no data path into OC's
ordinary candidate crossbars, saved-source registers or OC/EX registers.
The formatted load's functional data fanout ends at MEM/WB read_data.

OC still resolves nearest qualified EX, MEM, WB and ID producers in
the current age order. A matching MEM load becomes available only on
its actual acceptance cycle. If OC advances on that edge, mark each
source selecting this accepted load with a registered load-bank bit
in OC/EX and store a harmless placeholder in that source's ordinary
operand slot. Every other source is captured normally through the
existing flattened crossbar. Only the current MEM-load selection can
create a new OC/EX reference; saved sources have their existing priority.
The consumer enters EX on the same edge that the load bank receives
its exact value. Thus an immediate load consumer retains one dependency
bubble, rather than paying the r10 second bubble. The reference bit
qualifies data, never a speculative memory acceptance or instruction.

In EX, resolve each architectural source using a single two-input mux
between its ordinary OC/EX register and the registered load bank. Use the same
registered source reference for the corresponding prepared ALU role
only when that role actually uses the source: AUIPC still uses its PC
and immediate operations still use their immediate. Branches, JALR,
effective addresses, store data, narrow multiply prediction, divider
launch and EX/MEM RVFI source snapshots all consume the resolved exact
sources. Do not reintroduce EX/MEM/WB tag comparisons or a general
forwarding network before EX arithmetic. The new two-way bank mux is
the explicit timing tradeoff against the removed live-bus OC path.

A bank reference is valid for the first EX cycle after OC capture.
When EX advances, its fully resolved payload goes into EX/MEM before
any simultaneous MEM/WB update can overwrite the shared bank. If OC/EX
is held, materialize every referenced value into that instruction's
ordinary architectural and applicable ALU operand registers on the
first held edge and clear those reference bits. Preserve all other
held metadata. Materialization has priority over ordinary hold but
loses to reset and redirect; it is an internal operand update, not
instruction advancement. This includes downstream dmem stalls and
divider occupancy. Divider launch snapshots resolved operands and
its original payload exactly once; later bank writes cannot alter
an active divider, its bypass result or its RVFI source records.

Preserve independently saved OC operands when OC cannot advance.
For an unsaved source selecting a currently accepted MEM load, save
a one-cycle pending-load bit instead of its live data. In the next
cycle the pending source reads the registered load bank as its saved
candidate. On the next edge, either capture that exact registered
value into the advancing OC/EX ordinary slot, or materialize it into
the saved-source value register and clear the pending bit while OC
stays held. Nonblocking updates read the bank's pre-edge value, even
when MEM/WB changes on that edge. Never carry an older pending
reference into EX as a new-load reference: one source can require the
previous bank value while the other references the load accepted on
this edge. Both sources selecting the same current load may share
the new bank reference. Saved values remain immutable until their
instruction advances or is flushed.

Keep unavailable-nearest-writer blocking, x0, target/access traps,
writer qualification, genuine dmem backpressure and stable requests.
Preserve EX ordinary-result return and MEM registered nonload bypass,
full-rate dependent ALU issue, all existing branch prediction and
recovery, multiplier validation/repair/quarantine and divider control.
Older multiply repair suppresses new references and clears all younger
references and pending saved sources. Reset initializes MEM/WB and
reference validity; invalid or flushed references have no effects.
Preserve default-illegal decoding, SYSTEM policy, real and ALTOPS
arithmetic, nret=1, all external ports, original RVFI addresses/data,
memory records, PC successors and consecutive retirement order.

The expected eight-percent fitness gain has low confidence. Scheduling
should retain the champion's load-use and normal dependent-ALU timing,
but the added EX bank mux may make arithmetic or recovery the new
limit. Require (Fmax_new/91.186)*(4196601/cycles_new) > 1.046 using
unchanged CoreMark CRC/UART/MMIO-bracket validation and all three Gowin
placements. At identical cycles, acceptance needs median Fmax above
95.381 MHz; eight percent needs about 98.481 MHz. These are targets,
not measured results. Run unchanged formal, all affected unit suites
and ready/stalled field-by-field trace cosim. Do not alter any evaluator,
wrapper, benchmark, stall generator, formal bound or another core.

title: Untagged synchronous load-value prediction with use-qualified replay
motivation: The champion scores 217.29 at 91.186 MHz with 4,196,601 measured CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent. Relevant predictor attempts were reviewed, especially r9s2's tagged load-history predictor, which regressed timing despite good coverage. Isolated local probes found that a small late table still adds a long OC path; a large early table needs synchronous byte-bank reads to avoid thousands of registers. With that mapping fixed, the tagged prototype reached 81.471 MHz in placement option 0 and its worst path was the tag memory through MEM qualification to OC, with 29 cells. The most promising remaining load-predictor angle is to remove tags entirely and register the predicted word before MEM, validating only predictions actually captured by OC.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one advisory 128-entry raw-word load-value predictor indexed by word-address bits [8:2]. Each entry stores only 32 data bits and validity: no address tags, address-hit comparison, cached permissions or coherence assumptions. Index aliases are permitted prediction errors and are always checked before affected younger instructions can retire.

Read the predictor synchronously on the EX/MEM acceptance edge. EX derives the exact seven-bit word index using the low nine bits of its registered architectural rs1 plus immediate. Organize data as four independently writable 128-by-8 byte banks with simple synchronous read outputs and no data reset. Use a separate validity plane; reset table validity and the captured candidate-valid flag. The predictor's registered raw-word output and candidate validity form a sidecar to EX/MEM, rather than embedding resettable candidate-data flops in the wide EX/MEM struct. Capture both on the same enabled edge as the actual load address; hold both during dmem stalls. Gate read capture by advancing EX, excluding older recovery and divider wait; div completion and bubbles may read irrelevant candidates safely. Do not add a pipeline stage or move load availability into EX. Ensure the vendor infers memory and its output registers; the prior asynchronous-capture probe produced excessive flops.

In MEM, format that registered raw candidate with the load's actual lane, width and signedness. A valid candidate is available only for a valid legal aligned nonzero-destination load on its real dmemReady handshake and current writer eligibility. Do not perform an address-tag check. Keep EX loads unavailable, preserving the current one-bubble load-use timing on warm candidates. Cold invalid slots leave the nearest MEM producer unavailable until exact WB; never fall back to live dmemRData on the MEM-to-OC path. Arbitrary candidate contents may exist while invalid, but cannot be captured as a ready architectural source.

Expose a one-cycle OC indication that a MEM source is actually captured. It is true when a valid nonflushed OC instruction captures an unsaved, ready source selected from MEM, whether into OC/EX on advance or into a saved source while held. Check both raw register source fields, preserving the current operand and RVFI conventions. Already saved sources do not count again; unavailable MEM sources never count; reset and older recovery suppress capture. This indication observes existing selections and capture conditions and must not change forwarding, hazard readiness or source selection.

Every load still performs its original bus transaction and commits the exact formatted bus result and raw RVFI memory data. Compare the captured candidate raw word against actual dmemRData only for an accepted valid legal aligned load with a nonzero destination. Register replay when candidate-valid, OC captured a MEM source, and the words differ. Full-word equality suffices for all load widths and signs; differences in unused bytes may conservatively replay. An unused wrong candidate needs no repair because no younger operand contains it. Retire the original load exactly once with the exact value in either case. Keep equality and the use indication off current bypass readiness, frontend control and memory enables; they feed the recovery register only.

OR this load mismatch with the existing independently qualified multiply mismatch at MEM/WB. Reuse the current original pc_next recovery target and next-cycle older repair priority. Quarantine younger MEM requests even if unready, squash younger EX/OC/decode and saved operands, suppress younger redirect/training, and cancel younger divider state or held completion. This also handles a predicted source saved while an unrelated younger division holds EX. All younger work that could contain a consumed wrong prediction is discarded before retirement or a memory side effect.

Learn once from accepted legal aligned nonquarantined MEM transactions, independent of whether the current candidate was used or right. Loads and full-word stores fill all four banks and validate their indexed slot. Partial stores update their enabled byte banks only when that indexed slot is already valid; do not allocate unknown remaining bytes on an invalid slot. With no tags, a partial store may merge bytes belonging to another address: that result remains an arbitrary advisory candidate and is safe only through exact validation. Never treat the history as a memory cache or suppress a bus read. Qualify writes with real readiness, enabled memory operation, !hold_wb, !older_recovery and !reset. Keep synchronous pre-write read semantics on same-index load/store edges; stale early candidates are expected and recover when used.

The intended benefit is a short registered candidate-to-OC data path and a one-bit validity qualification, eliminating live BRAM return timing and full-tag qualification. Compared with r9s2, lookup is one edge earlier, data banks infer synchronous FPGA memory, tags are absent and recovery is use-qualified. No tag miss waiting remains after warmup. Costs are extra memory blocks, byte-formatting logic, raw-word mismatch replays, cold waits and the remaining EX-result return path. Aliasing accuracy and store-read timing must be measured in RTL; sequential history coverage does not establish this candidate's accuracy or fitness. Do not assume loaded values, address ranges, memory stability or predictor correctness in formal builds.

Preserve nret=1 and all external ports, existing branch prediction, exact real and ALTOPS arithmetic, decoder defaults and reserved-encoding traps, bus handshakes, alignment behavior, nearest producer priority, source retention, original RVFI operands/results/memory/PC/order, and every hard invariant. Run unchanged formal, directed candidate/capture/recovery tests, ready and stalled trace cosims, canonical 2K CoreMark CRC/MMIO/bracket/completion/bounded-access checks, and median vendor Gowin timing. Require (Fmax_new/91.186)*(4196601/cycles_new) > 1.046. Expected gain is an estimate with low confidence, not a measured win.

title: Fold EX result classes directly into OC forwarding masks
motivation:
The champion achieves 217.29 fitness at median Gowin Fmax 91.186 MHz
with 4,196,601 bracketed CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent; the
micro_opt history and recent outcomes were reviewed. A fresh baseline
timing run reproduced 87.616/91.186/91.186 MHz. In placement options
1 and 2 the worst path starts at an EX ALU operation register, crosses
the inferred arithmetic and OC data selection, and ends at the narrow
multiplier's absorbed operand register. EX currently selects jump link,
predicted product or ordinary ALU result before OC selects that producer.
The r9 improvement removed serial saved-source and ALU-role muxes in OC,
but left this upstream EX result-selection boundary intact.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make one local exact micro-optimization: absorb EX's outer result-class
selection into OC's existing mutually exclusive forwarding masks.
Preserve every pipeline stage, advancement edge, bus handshake and
prediction policy. Do not register a new result or add a dependency
bubble. The intended physical change is removal of the serial wide
jump/multiply selections between EX arithmetic and OC capture.

Export three unselected EX candidates: the existing ordinary ALU
result, the existing predicted multiplication result, and PC+4 link.
Also export the current registered instruction's is_jump and is_mul
classifications. Keep the existing final, post-trap bypass_w_en and
bypass_ready authoritative. The ordinary candidate includes the held
divider result exactly as today; it must not become usable before the
existing divider completion. No new arithmetic or prediction is added.

For each OC destination role, replace its single masked ex_value term
with three disjoint terms. If E is that role's existing EX select, use
E && is_jump for the link, E && !is_jump && is_mul for the product, and
E && !is_jump && !is_mul for the ordinary ALU result. Form these scalar
enables before the wide data masks, then combine the three candidates
directly with that role's saved, MEM, WB, ID and PC/immediate candidates
in its final OR reduction. For ALU A/B, E already incorporates the
existing AUIPC/immediate restrictions. Jump selection must retain its
current precedence. Use balanced reductions; do not reconstruct a
shared selected EX word followed by another role mux, or an EX-only
wide reduction followed by the original producer-selection mux.

Apply the same expanded architectural-source networks to one-time
saved-source capture. Preserve saved-source precedence, strict nearest
EX-over-MEM-over-WB-over-ID priority, unavailable-producer blocking,
x0, independently retained operands and all capture/hold/reset/flush
rules. The scalar producer and result-class selects must describe the
same current EX instruction as the candidate data. Preserve full-rate
dependent ALU issue and the accepted-load single dependency bubble.
Keep MEM load formatting and its complete bypass interface unchanged.

EX/MEM still captures the original selected result on its existing
edge; its payload, divider transactions and cancellation, exact MEM
multiplication validation, registered repair and younger-memory
quarantine remain intact. Keep all target/address arithmetic, branch
comparison, prediction, redirects, training, alignment traps, decoder
default-illegal validation and SYSTEM policy. Preserve real/ALTOPS
arithmetic, nret=1, every external port, exact RVFI source snapshots,
results, successors, memory records and consecutive retirement order.
Change only the listed allowed RTL and cocotb files.

Expect an eight-percent fitness gain with low confidence and unchanged
counted cycles. This final EX-to-OC fusion has not been implemented or
measured. Do not substitute the measured rejected probes: balanced
byte comparisons reached 77.661 MHz median, a shared signed multiplier
81.350 MHz, registered multiplier sign bits 81.642 MHz, a dedicated
ADD/SUB control 79.475 MHz, branch predicate factoring 82.037 MHz and

selector also regressed; this proposal instead removes the EX/OC
selection boundary while retaining binary ALU decoding and arithmetic.

formatting into OC, whereas this change adds only two EX result terms.

MEM-return path can outweigh the removed muxes. Inspect the Gowin mapped

without an intermediate class-selected data word. Require

cosim, canonical CoreMark CRC/UART/MMIO-bracket checks and all three
vendor Gowin placements. Preserve every architectural and advancement
assertion; report actual cycles and median fitness before claiming a win.

title: Retimed synchronous register-file banks with collision bypass folded into OC
motivation:
The champion scores 217.29 at 91.186 MHz and 4,196,601 measured
CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent. The structural history was
reviewed: r8s1 improved fitness by separating operand collection from
execution, while r10s1's extra load-return stage and r14s1's post-OC
load-bank mux regressed. r9s0 improved the champion by folding operand
selection into parallel capture masks. r5s0's flop register file also
regressed. These results favor using existing register boundaries and
flattened capture selection rather than adding execution-input muxes.

Isolated fetch-buffer probes passed ready/stalled traces and canonical
CoreMark checks but lost too much Gowin frequency. A synchronous
register-file prototype preserved exactly 4,196,601 CoreMark cycles and
passed all eight selftest/random-program ready/stalled trace comparisons.
However, its registered write-first/validity output mux precedes the
existing OC capture crossbar. A padded-memory variant measured only
83.546 MHz median, so that prototype is a regression and is not the
proposed final circuit. The promising remaining structural refinement is
to move those snapshot selections into OC's existing scalar route masks.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the asynchronous register file plus separate ID operand
snapshot flops with two replicated synchronous read banks, using the
existing ID-to-OC capture edge as the memory read boundary. Broadcast
the sole WB write to both banks. Read the incoming decoded instruction's
rs1 and rs2 addresses on exactly the edge that captures its ID/OC
metadata. Hold the registered bank outputs whenever ID/OC is held.
There is no additional instruction stage, dependency bubble, load-return
stage or mux after OC/EX. Keep all EX, MEM, WB and divider behavior at
the champion's boundaries.

Expose the raw registered bank words directly to OC. Also capture and
hold, on that same decode edge, each source's nonzero/initialized bit,
each source's WB write-collision bit, and one shared 32-bit WB write
value. Use a resettable 32-bit initialized plane instead of resetting
RAM contents: reset clears logical register validity, accepted nonzero
writes set the corresponding bit, and both replicas receive identical
writes. Capture the pre-edge initialized state and explicitly handle
same-edge WB writes. A same-edge matching nonzero write selects the
captured WB value even when that register was previously uninitialized.
An uninitialized noncolliding register and x0 select zero. Raw RAM data
may be unknown while invalid, but must never appear in a valid operand.
Do not rely on a device-specific read-during-write result or RAM power-up
contents. Reset and recovery discard snapshot ownership through the
existing instruction-valid and saved-source rules.

Crucially, do not reconstruct a write-first architectural snapshot with
a 32-bit collision/zero mux between the RAM output and operand_stage.
Fold this selection into the existing mutually exclusive OC capture
masks. Preserve saved-source priority and qualified EX, MEM, WB nearest
producer priority. Only when the existing forwarding route selects the
ID snapshot may its data split into two parallel terms: raw registered
bank data masked by nonzero, initialized and !collision; or the shared
captured WB value masked by nonzero and collision. If neither term is
eligible, the source is zero. Live EX/MEM/WB routes must suppress both
ID terms. A matching unavailable nearest producer must still block
capture instead of falling back to any snapshot. Saved sources remain
authoritative after their producer or collision snapshot drains.

Apply the same flattened masks directly to all four current capture
roles: architectural rs1, architectural rs2, prepared ALU a and prepared
ALU b. PC and immediate remain parallel terms using existing role masks.
The ordinary resolved-source network used for independent retention
must also consume the raw/collision candidates directly. Never feed a
completed snapshot mux into a second operand mux. Every role still ends
at the existing OC/EX flops; EX arithmetic receives the same already
resolved operands as the champion. Preserve full-rate dependent ordinary
ALU issue and the current one-bubble immediate load-use schedule.

Pair raw bank outputs and all snapshot metadata with the exact ID/OC
instruction across advances and holds. The bank read enable, snapshot
flags and captured collision value share the existing ID/OC acceptance
condition, including captures into an empty decoded slot during an older
EX hold. Do not infer an extra RAM output-register stage. Ignore bank
reads on discarded recovery-edge payloads, and ensure the first target
instruction obtains a fresh matched read on its own decode edge. Eliminate
the now redundant ID rs-value data registers and unused ID-prepared
operand copies from the timed datapath. Keep original architectural
source addresses and exact resolved source values for RVFI.

Use ordinary synthesizable synchronous memory semantics in simulation
and formal. Map the replicated banks to native Gowin block memory if
possible, with an appropriate declaration/attribute and physical depth
padding when needed. Verify actual inference in the vendor report;
declaring an attribute alone is insufficient. Any device-specific
implementation must have an equivalent unrestricted formal/simulation
model, with the same enabled-read latency, holds, writes, logical reset
and explicit collision bypass. Never assume away read collisions or
uninitialized addresses. Do not modify synthesis scripts or wrappers.

This is one structural retiming of register-file storage, write-first
snapshot handling and operand capture. The expected eight-percent gain
has low confidence and is not measured. The earlier straightforward
synchronous prototype regressed; the final flattened raw-bank/collision
capture has not been built or timed. Its intended benefit is removal of
the additional snapshot mux while reducing asynchronous read routing and
resettable operand storage. Remaining live MEM-load and EX-result return
paths can still dominate, and extra mask fanout or memory placement can
negate the gain. Acceptance requires

title: Retirement-trained return-address prediction with exact EX target repair
motivation:
The champion scores 217.29 at 91.186 MHz with 4,196,601 bracketed
CoreMark cycles. LESSONS.md is absent. Predictor history includes
successful bimodal/JAL prediction, but delayed control validation,
branch-table recoding, folded indexing and load-value prediction lost
fitness. Every JALR still redirects in EX, including ordinary returns.
Return addresses depend on the calling context, so a small return stack
can predict them more accurately than the last-target table used in
r8s2 without delaying conditional-branch resolution or touching OC data.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add one eight-entry retirement-trained return-address stack (RAS).
Push the architectural PC+4 of retiring legal aligned JAL/JALR calls
whose destination is x1 or x5. Pop for retiring legal aligned JALR
instructions with a link-register source and a different destination;
implement the standard RISC-V push/pop hint table, including pop-then-
push when distinct link registers are used. Saturate occupancy at eight,
discard the oldest address on overflow, and keep an empty pop harmless.
Reset occupancy; invalid storage must never influence a prediction.

Train only from the current valid MEM/WB retirement payload, using its
exact trap state and original instruction, PC and architectural source
values. Do not update the stack at fetch or EX. Thus wrong-path calls
and returns, held instructions, divider waits and younger multiplication
repair cannot corrupt stack state, and no checkpoint or rollback bank
is needed. A legal older retirement still updates the RAS during its
younger-instruction repair. Pre-edge stack contents supply lookup on a
simultaneous training and fetch-acceptance edge.

Predict only canonical returns: legal raw JALR encoding, rd=x0,
rs1 in {x1,x5}, immediate=0, and nonempty RAS. Use the aligned top return
address directly as the fetch successor. On empty or unqualified lookup,
retain the current sequential JALR fetch policy. Preserve all existing
conditional-direction and immediate-JAL prediction logic and EX timing.
Couple consumption to the existing fetch_accept edge. Capture a separate
return-prediction-valid bit and predicted target with the accepted
instruction through IF/ID, ID/OC and OC/EX; retain these metadata through
stalls and clear them on reset/flush exactly like predicted_taken.

Resolve every JALR from the exact registered architectural rs1 and
immediate in EX, clearing bit zero as today. For an aligned legal JALR,
skip redirect only when its captured return prediction is valid and
equals the actual target; otherwise use the existing EX redirect and
squash priority. Keep conditional direction-XOR recovery unchanged.
Resolve misaligned JALR traps exactly, suppress its link write and
repair to PC+4 if a captured return prediction diverted fetch. Maintain
actual RVFI pc_next independently of prediction. A wrong RAS entry or
stale top therefore affects only performance, never architectural state.

This predictor targets the remaining return redirect bubbles. Committed
training intentionally trades some close-call/return misses for small
state and simple recovery; those misses must be measured. Keep the RAS
lookup separate from branch-direction lookup, and avoid adding a generic
full-width successor comparison to ordinary EX instructions. Do not add
a BTB, global history, load prediction, extra pipeline stage or arithmetic
prediction. Preserve nret=1, every external port, exact real and ALTOPS
arithmetic, decode legality, memory handshakes, source retention, older
multiply repair, divider cancellation, RVFI fields/order and all checks.

Run unchanged formal and ready/stalled trace cosim, directed RAS and
pipeline recovery tests, canonical 2K CoreMark CRC/MMIO/bracket/completion
validation and median vendor Gowin timing. Compare actual prediction
hits, misses and cycles rather than equating architectural return counts
with RTL savings. Require (Fmax_new/91.186)*(4196601/cycles_new) > 1.046.
The six-percent expected fitness gain is an unmeasured estimate with low
confidence because target comparison, late committed updates and routing
can limit the benefit.
